glycerin.name: Glycerin
glycerin.body: Glycerin helps your skin hold onto water. That can leave dry skin feeling softer and more comfortable.
glycerin.detail: This type of ingredient is called a humectant. It works alongside oils and other ingredients that soften skin and help slow water loss.
glycerin.evidence: Its water-holding role and moisturizing benefits are well established.

squalane.name: Squalane
squalane.summary: Softens skin and slows moisture loss
squalane.body: Squalane softens dry, rough skin and leaves a thin layer that helps slow water loss. It can make skin feel smoother and more supple.
squalane.detail: A skin-softening ingredient like this is called an emollient. Squalane is related to squalene, a fat naturally found in skin, but is more resistant to breaking down through contact with oxygen. How heavy a lotion feels depends on the whole mixture.
squalane.evidence: Its skin-softening and moisture-retaining roles are well established.

caprylic-capric-triglyceride.name: Caprylic/Capric Triglyceride
caprylic-capric-triglyceride.summary: Softens skin and helps lotion spread
caprylic-capric-triglyceride.body: This oily ingredient makes skin feel smoother and helps lotion spread easily. It is a useful part of a moisturizer for dry skin.
caprylic-capric-triglyceride.detail: It is often made using coconut-derived ingredients, but it is different from coconut oil. Its name alone cannot tell you whether a finished lotion will feel greasy or cause breakouts.
caprylic-capric-triglyceride.evidence: Its skin-softening and spreading roles are well established.

hyaluronic-acid.name: Hyaluronic Acid
hyaluronic-acid.summary: Holds water at the skin’s surface
hyaluronic-acid.body: Hyaluronic acid holds water at the skin’s surface. That can help skin feel hydrated and look temporarily smoother.
hyaluronic-acid.detail: Different sizes of the molecule can be used in skincare. The ingredient name does not reveal which sizes or how much are in a product, so it cannot establish deeper penetration or lasting wrinkle improvement.
hyaluronic-acid.evidence: Its water-holding role is well established. The amount and molecule size affect how it works.

sodium-hyaluronate.name: Sodium Hyaluronate
sodium-hyaluronate.summary: Helps keep the skin’s surface hydrated
sodium-hyaluronate.body: Sodium hyaluronate is a form of hyaluronic acid that helps skin hold water. It can make the surface feel hydrated and smoother.
sodium-hyaluronate.detail: It is the salt form of hyaluronic acid, a related but distinct ingredient. Different molecule sizes can be used. Neither name on a label tells you which product will moisturize better.
sodium-hyaluronate.evidence: Its water-holding role is well established. The naming difference does not prove better absorption or results.

pentylene-glycol.name: Pentylene Glycol
pentylene-glycol.summary: Helps hold water and protect the lotion
pentylene-glycol.body: Pentylene glycol helps skin hold water and helps other ingredients dissolve. It can also help protect the lotion from spoiling.
pentylene-glycol.detail: One ingredient can do several jobs in the same product. Here, it can contribute to both skin comfort and the way the lotion stays usable in its bottle.
pentylene-glycol.evidence: Its dissolving and formulation roles are recognized. The reference also reports moisturizing and skin-feel properties from ingredient-supplier information.

caprylyl-glycol.name: Caprylyl Glycol
caprylyl-glycol.summary: Softens skin and helps protect the lotion
caprylyl-glycol.body: Caprylyl glycol helps skin feel soft and hold moisture. It also helps the ingredients that protect the lotion from spoiling work better.
caprylyl-glycol.detail: Those protective ingredients are called preservatives. Caprylyl glycol can give them a boost, so its job extends beyond how the lotion feels on your skin.
caprylyl-glycol.evidence: Its moisturizing, skin-softening and preservative-boosting roles are recognized.

hexanediol.name: 1,2-Hexanediol
hexanediol.summary: Helps hold water and protect the lotion
hexanediol.body: It helps ingredients dissolve and can help skin hold water and feel soft. It also supports the ingredients that protect the lotion from spoiling.
hexanediol.detail: It can support the ingredients that control unwanted microbes, such as bacteria. A small amount can still do a useful job in the product, even when it appears near the end of the ingredient list.
hexanediol.evidence: Its dissolving, water-holding, skin-softening and preservative-support roles are recognized.

ethylhexylglycerin.name: Ethylhexylglycerin
ethylhexylglycerin.body: Ethylhexylglycerin helps preservatives protect the lotion from spoiling. It can also add a soft feel on skin.
ethylhexylglycerin.detail: Preservatives help keep unwanted microbes from growing in a product during storage and use. Despite its name, ethylhexylglycerin is different from glycerin, which is mainly known for helping skin hold water.
ethylhexylglycerin.evidence: Its preservative-boosting and skin-care roles are recognized.

niacinamide.name: Niacinamide
niacinamide.body: Niacinamide is a form of vitamin B3 that can support the skin’s outer protective layer. This layer, called the skin barrier, helps keep moisture in.
niacinamide.detail: It can support the skin’s own production of protective fats. A small human study found less water escaping from skin treated with niacinamide-containing products. If a product irritates you, that reaction alone does not identify niacinamide as the cause.
niacinamide.evidence: A 28-day study in 20 healthy volunteers found improved moisture-barrier measures. It did not test current US CeraVe PM or establish its niacinamide amount.

cholesterol.name: Cholesterol
cholesterol.summary: Adds a fat used in skin’s protective layer
cholesterol.body: Cholesterol is one of the fats in skin’s outer protective layer, which helps keep moisture in. In a moisturizer, it also helps soften skin.
cholesterol.detail: These skin fats are called lipids. Their amounts and how they work together matter, as well as which ingredients are present.
cholesterol.evidence: Its role in the skin’s protective layer and its skin-softening use are established. Product results depend on the whole mixture.

phytosphingosine.name: Phytosphingosine
phytosphingosine.summary: Adds a building block of skin fats
phytosphingosine.body: Phytosphingosine is a building block found in some of the fats in skin’s outer layer. It is used in skincare to help keep skin in good condition.
phytosphingosine.detail: Early research also looks at effects on microbes and inflammation. Those findings are interesting, but they do not show that a moisturizer containing it will treat acne.
phytosphingosine.evidence: Its role as a skin-fat building block is established. Evidence for additional skin benefits is more limited.

ceramide-eop.name: Ceramide EOP
ceramide-eop.summary: Adds a skin fat that helps keep water in
ceramide-eop.body: Ceramide EOP is a type of fat found in skin’s outer protective layer. In a moisturizer, it is used to support that layer and help skin keep moisture in.
ceramide-eop.detail: It is also known by the older name Ceramide 1. Ceramides work within a mixture of skin fats; their amount and how they are combined matter as well as their names.
ceramide-eop.evidence: The role of ceramides in skin is established. An ingredient list does not show how well the complete product supports that protective layer.
ceramide-eop.aliasNotes: It is also known by the older name Ceramide 1. Ceramides work within a mixture of skin fats; their amount and how they are combined matter as well as their names.

ceramide-np.name: Ceramide NP
ceramide-np.summary: Adds a skin fat that helps retain moisture
ceramide-np.body: Ceramide NP is another fat used to support skin’s outer protective layer. That layer helps stop moisture from escaping too quickly.
ceramide-np.detail: NP, AP and EOP name different types of ceramides. The letters are not quality grades. Ceramides work with other fats and moisturizing ingredients, so more ceramide names do not automatically mean a better product.
ceramide-np.evidence: Research on ceramides and ceramide mixtures supports this role. It does not isolate NP’s effect in either lotion.

ceramide-ap.name: Ceramide AP
ceramide-ap.summary: Supports the skin layer that holds moisture
ceramide-ap.body: Ceramide AP is a fat used to support skin’s outer protective layer. It is one part of the mixture that helps skin hold onto moisture.
ceramide-ap.detail: AP names a particular type of ceramide. It works alongside other skin fats, water-holding ingredients and skin softeners. Its presence adds to the formula’s makeup without proving a separate extra benefit.
ceramide-ap.evidence: The role of the ceramide family is established. A unique benefit from AP in either lotion is not established.

ceramide-ng.name: Ceramide NG
ceramide-ng.summary: Adds another fat used in skin’s outer layer
ceramide-ng.body: Ceramide NG is a type of skin-related fat used to support the outer layer that keeps moisture in. It works as part of a moisturizer’s wider mix of ingredients.
ceramide-ng.detail: It belongs to the ceramide family, but has its own chemical structure. An additional ceramide can be a useful part of a blend; counting its name does not tell us how much extra benefit the blend provides.
ceramide-ng.evidence: The reference describes the ceramide family’s role. It does not establish a separate NG-specific result in this product.

ceramide-as.name: Ceramide AS
ceramide-as.summary: Helps keep skin in good condition
ceramide-as.body: Ceramide AS is a skin-related fat used to help keep skin in good condition. It belongs to the same broad family as the other ceramides in this lotion.
ceramide-as.detail: Its basic role is documented, but there is less direct detail about what AS alone adds. That supports a modest skin-care description rather than a promise of a specific repair benefit.
ceramide-as.evidence: Its identity and skin-care use are documented. The reviewed AS-specific benefit evidence is limited.

phytosterols.name: Phytosterols
phytosterols.summary: Plant ingredients used to care for skin
phytosterols.body: Phytosterols are substances from plants used to help keep skin in good condition. They can form part of a moisturizer’s mix of skin-care fats.
phytosterols.detail: They belong to a group called sterols. Being plant-derived does not by itself make an ingredient safer or more effective. The reviewed evidence supports their skin-care role without establishing a separate repair benefit.
phytosterols.evidence: Their plant origin and skin-care use are documented. Specific clinical benefit evidence in the reviewed reference is limited.

glyceryl-stearate.name: Glyceryl Stearate
glyceryl-stearate.summary: Softens skin and gives lotion a creamy feel
glyceryl-stearate.body: Glyceryl stearate softens skin and helps give the lotion a creamy texture. It also helps the oily and watery ingredients stay mixed.
glyceryl-stearate.detail: An ingredient that helps oil and water stay together is called an emulsifier. This one contributes both to the skin feel and to the structure of the lotion.
glyceryl-stearate.evidence: Its skin-softening and mixing roles are well established.

stearyl-alcohol.name: Stearyl Alcohol
stearyl-alcohol.summary: Softens skin and thickens the lotion
stearyl-alcohol.body: Stearyl alcohol is a waxy ingredient that softens skin and thickens the lotion. It helps keep the oily and watery ingredients together.
stearyl-alcohol.detail: It is a fatty alcohol, which behaves differently from the quick-drying alcohol in some toners. The word alcohol alone does not tell you that an ingredient will dry out skin.
stearyl-alcohol.evidence: Its skin-softening, thickening and mixing roles are well established.

cetearyl-alcohol.name: Cetearyl Alcohol
cetearyl-alcohol.summary: Makes lotion creamy and skin feel softer
cetearyl-alcohol.body: Cetearyl alcohol helps lotion feel creamy and spread smoothly. It also softens skin and helps the ingredients stay mixed.
cetearyl-alcohol.detail: It is a mixture of waxy fatty alcohols. These behave differently from ethanol, the quick-drying alcohol used in some products. Their useful jobs here are softness and texture.
cetearyl-alcohol.evidence: Its skin-softening and mixing roles are well established.

polyglyceryl-2-stearate.name: Polyglyceryl-2 Stearate
polyglyceryl-2-stearate.body: Polyglyceryl-2 stearate helps the lotion’s oily and watery ingredients stay mixed. That keeps them together as one product you can spread over your skin.
polyglyceryl-2-stearate.detail: This kind of ingredient is called an emulsifier. Its useful job is inside the bottle: helping the moisturizer stay evenly blended.
polyglyceryl-2-stearate.evidence: Its mixing role is documented. The reference does not provide clinical skin-benefit studies.

polyglyceryl-3-diisostearate.name: Polyglyceryl-3 Diisostearate
polyglyceryl-3-diisostearate.summary: Helps the lotion stay evenly mixed
polyglyceryl-3-diisostearate.body: Polyglyceryl-3 diisostearate helps oily and watery ingredients stay together. It also contributes to how the lotion spreads and feels.
polyglyceryl-3-diisostearate.detail: This is another emulsifier, the name for an ingredient that helps oil and water stay mixed. It is different from polyglyceryl-2 stearate even though their broad jobs sound similar.

hydrogenated-lecithin.name: Hydrogenated Lecithin
hydrogenated-lecithin.summary: Helps ingredients mix and skin feel soft
hydrogenated-lecithin.body: Hydrogenated lecithin helps oily and watery ingredients work together. It can also help skin feel soft and keep other ingredients stable.
hydrogenated-lecithin.detail: It belongs to a group of fat-based ingredients. Some related ingredients are used to carry other ingredients in tiny structures, but this name on a label does not prove that a product uses a special delivery system.
hydrogenated-lecithin.evidence: Its skin-softening and mixing roles are established. A special delivery claim would need product-specific evidence.

ceteareth-20.name: Ceteareth-20
ceteareth-20.summary: Keeps the lotion’s oil and water together
ceteareth-20.body: Ceteareth-20 helps oil and water stay mixed in the lotion. That helps the product keep a consistent texture.
ceteareth-20.detail: It is an emulsifier. It works where the oily and watery parts meet, helping keep oil spread throughout the lotion rather than separating into a layer.
ceteareth-20.evidence: Its mixing role is well established.

behentrimonium-methosulfate.name: Behentrimonium Methosulfate
behentrimonium-methosulfate.summary: Helps make a smooth, well-mixed lotion
behentrimonium-methosulfate.body: This ingredient helps the lotion stay mixed and spread smoothly. It works with waxy ingredients to give the product a consistent texture.
behentrimonium-methosulfate.detail: Its name includes methosulfate, but it is different from the foaming sulfate cleansers people often mean when discussing harsh sulfates. Its role here is mixing and skin feel.
behentrimonium-methosulfate.evidence: Its mixing and skin-feel uses are recognized.

sodium-lauroyl-lactylate.name: Sodium Lauroyl Lactylate
sodium-lauroyl-lactylate.summary: Helps keep the lotion evenly mixed
sodium-lauroyl-lactylate.body: Sodium lauroyl lactylate helps oily and watery ingredients stay mixed. It can also support the ingredients that protect the lotion from spoiling.
sodium-lauroyl-lactylate.detail: It works alongside other mixing ingredients. Together, they help a moisturizer remain one consistent product through storage and use.
sodium-lauroyl-lactylate.evidence: Its mixing and preservative-support roles are recognized.

carbomer.name: Carbomer
carbomer.body: Carbomer gives a lotion or gel its thickness. That makes the product easier to dispense and spread.
carbomer.detail: It is a large-molecule ingredient called a polymer. It helps build a consistent texture, but its name alone cannot predict heaviness or pilling, the little rolls that sometimes form when products are rubbed or layered.
carbomer.evidence: Its thickening and texture-stabilizing roles are established.

xanthan-gum.name: Xanthan Gum
xanthan-gum.summary: Helps the lotion keep its texture
xanthan-gum.body: Xanthan gum helps control how thick the lotion is and how easily it flows. It also helps keep ingredients spread evenly through the product.
xanthan-gum.detail: It works with other texture-building ingredients. The finished mixture determines the feel, so xanthan gum on a label does not necessarily mean a lotion will feel thick or sticky.
xanthan-gum.evidence: Its thickening and texture-stabilizing roles are established.

polyacrylate-crosspolymer-11.name: Polyacrylate Crosspolymer-11
polyacrylate-crosspolymer-11.summary: Controls thickness and helps prevent separation
polyacrylate-crosspolymer-11.body: This ingredient helps the lotion keep its intended thickness. It also helps stop the oily and watery parts from separating.
polyacrylate-crosspolymer-11.detail: It is a polymer, a type of large-molecule ingredient used here to build texture. Small amounts of texture helpers can still make a useful difference to how a lotion behaves.
polyacrylate-crosspolymer-11.evidence: Its thickening and mixture-stabilizing roles are documented.

water.name: Water
water.body: Water forms the lotion’s liquid base and dissolves some of its other ingredients. It helps turn the full mixture into a lotion that spreads over skin.
water.detail: Water is often first on a lotion’s ingredient list. The other ingredients help skin hold moisture and feel soft, so the water alone does not determine how moisturizing the product is.
water.evidence: Its role as a dissolving base is established. Water, Aqua and Eau are names for the same ingredient.
water.aliasNotes: Its role as a dissolving base is established. Water, Aqua and Eau are names for the same ingredient.

potassium-phosphate.name: Potassium Phosphate
potassium-phosphate.body: Potassium phosphate helps keep the lotion at its intended level of acidity. That helps the ingredients work together consistently.
potassium-phosphate.detail: Acidity is measured as pH. An ingredient that helps keep pH steady is called a buffer. The ingredient list does not tell us the lotion’s measured pH.

dipotassium-phosphate.name: Dipotassium Phosphate
dipotassium-phosphate.summary: Helps keep the lotion’s acidity steady
dipotassium-phosphate.body: Dipotassium phosphate helps stop the lotion’s acidity from changing too much. This supports a consistent product.
dipotassium-phosphate.detail: The acidity measure is called pH, and this pH-steadying job is called buffering. It is a different ingredient from potassium phosphate, although the two can work in the same formula.

disodium-edta.name: Disodium EDTA
disodium-edta.summary: Helps prevent unwanted changes in the lotion
disodium-edta.body: Disodium EDTA traps tiny traces of metals that could upset the lotion. That helps protect the product’s appearance and performance.
disodium-edta.detail: Those traces can come from water or raw ingredients. Capturing them is called chelation. This is a job inside the product, helping the rest of the mixture stay stable.
disodium-edta.evidence: Its metal-binding role is well established.

dimethicone.name: Dimethicone
dimethicone.summary: Softens skin and slows moisture loss
dimethicone.body: Dimethicone makes skin feel smoother and leaves a thin layer that helps slow water loss. It also helps the lotion glide over skin.
dimethicone.detail: It is a silicone, a family of ingredients used for smoothness and texture. Different types can feel light and silky or more substantial, so the complete product is the better guide to how heavy it feels.
dimethicone.evidence: Its skin-softening and moisture-retaining roles are established.

carnosine.name: Carnosine
carnosine.summary: Helps limit certain damaging chemical reactions
carnosine.body: In laboratory research, carnosine can help limit certain damaging chemical reactions, an effect called antioxidant activity. Whether it makes a visible difference to skin in this moisturizer is less clear.
carnosine.detail: It is a small peptide, made from two amino acids. Much of the promising research comes from laboratory or ingredient-supplier work. That is a reason to be interested, but it does not establish wrinkle reduction or more collagen from this lotion.
carnosine.evidence: Antioxidant activity is supported. A visible anti-ageing benefit from Vanicream is not established.

phenoxyethanol.name: Phenoxyethanol
phenoxyethanol.summary: Helps keep the lotion from spoiling
phenoxyethanol.body: Phenoxyethanol helps stop unwanted microbes, such as bacteria, from growing in the lotion. This helps protect the product during storage and use.
phenoxyethanol.detail: It is a preservative. A European scientific safety committee concluded it is safe for this use at amounts up to 1%. That is a safety assessment, not a measurement of how much is in CeraVe PM. A known personal allergy still matters.
phenoxyethanol.evidence: Its preservative role is established, with a formal SCCS safety assessment. Easily irritated skin alone does not identify a phenoxyethanol allergy.

panthenol.name: Panthenol
panthenol.body: Panthenol helps skin hold moisture and feel softer. It is a useful supporting ingredient in a moisturizer for dry skin.
panthenol.detail: You may see it called provitamin B5. Its water-holding job is called humectancy. It can also help ingredients dissolve, so it contributes both to skin feel and to how a product is made.
panthenol.evidence: Its water-holding, skin-conditioning and dissolving roles are documented in the published final cosmetic assessment.
panthenol.amountAndUse: The ingredient name does not give the amount or tell us whether the D form or a D-and-L mixture was used. Keep those details separate when comparing a product with research.
panthenol.aliasNotes: Pantothenol; pantothenyl alcohol. Dexpanthenol and D-panthenol identify the D form; preserve that detail instead of assuming every Panthenol label specifies it.
panthenol.distinctIngredients: Pantothenic acid, calcium pantothenate and panthenyl derivatives are separate ingredients.

allantoin.name: Allantoin
allantoin.summary: Helps soothe and care for skin
allantoin.body: Allantoin is used to help skin feel smoother and more comfortable. It is a useful supporting ingredient in products made to soothe skin.
allantoin.detail: Some US products also use allantoin as a labeled skin-protectant active. For example, the checked Skinfix ointment lists 0.5% allantoin and a skin-protectant purpose. That describes the specific ointment, not every cosmetic containing allantoin.
allantoin.evidence: Its soothing and skin-care roles are documented. The linked US ointment label separately identifies a skin-protectant purpose.
allantoin.amountAndUse: A cosmetic ingredient list may not show its amount. Do not use an example drug-label percentage as a universal target or assume that a higher amount will help more.
allantoin.aliasNotes: Allantoin; the chemical name (2,5-dioxo-4-imidazolidinyl)urea refers to this identity.
allantoin.distinctIngredients: Urea and complexes such as allantoin panthenol or allantoin ascorbate are separate identities.

urea.name: Urea
urea.summary: Holds water and softens dry, thick skin
urea.body: Urea helps skin hold water and can soften rough, thick surface skin. Its job changes with the strength and type of product.
urea.detail: Urea is one of the substances naturally involved in keeping the outer skin layer moist. More concentrated preparations can help loosen thick, built-up skin; that does not make them a better everyday moisturizer for every area.
urea.evidence: Moisture retention and softening thick surface skin are established uses.
urea.caution: Urea can sting. DermNet advises avoiding urea preparations on broken, infected or oozing skin; a stronger rough-skin product needs its own directions.
urea.amountAndUse: Check the percentage, body area and directions. A face moisturizer and a strong foot or nail preparation should not be treated as interchangeable because both say urea.
urea.distinctIngredients: Hydroxyethyl urea, diazolidinyl urea, imidazolidinyl urea and urea peroxide are distinct ingredients.

salicylic-acid.name: Salicylic Acid
salicylic-acid.summary: Loosens dead skin that can block pores
salicylic-acid.body: Salicylic acid helps loosen dead skin cells and clear surface buildup around pores. It appears in exfoliating skincare and products labeled to treat acne.
salicylic-acid.detail: It can have another job in a cosmetic: helping protect the product from spoiling. Seeing the name alone does not tell us whether a formula was designed for exfoliation, preservation or acne treatment.
salicylic-acid.evidence: Its dead-skin-shedding role is documented. The acne-treatment purpose and concurrent-treatment caution come from the identified US product label.
salicylic-acid.caution: The cited Clear Acne Face Moisturizer label warns that using another topical acne medicine at the same time or immediately afterward can increase dryness or irritation. Keep this as attributed label guidance; it is not a rule that all skincare combinations are incompatible.
salicylic-acid.amountAndUse: Check the active-ingredient percentage and whether the product is left on or rinsed off. An ingredient list alone does not give the amount or tell you how the product is meant to be used.
salicylic-acid.aliasNotes: o-Hydroxybenzoic acid. BHA is common skincare shorthand; alone, it is not specific enough for an exact ingredient match.
salicylic-acid.distinctIngredients: Sodium salicylate, betaine salicylate and capryloyl salicylic acid are separate ingredients.

glycolic-acid.name: Glycolic Acid
glycolic-acid.body: Glycolic acid can help dead cells shed from the skin’s surface, leaving it feeling smoother. It can also be used just to adjust a product’s acidity.
glycolic-acid.detail: It is an alpha hydroxy acid, usually shortened to AHA. This shedding process is called exfoliation. How much happens depends on the amount, the product’s acidity and the rest of its formula.
glycolic-acid.evidence: FDA explains the skin-shedding role and why the amount, acidity and whole formula matter.
glycolic-acid.caution: AHAs may increase sunburn sensitivity. FDA advises sunscreen, protective clothing and limiting sun exposure during use and for a week afterward. Irritation is also possible, especially with products that cause more exfoliation.
glycolic-acid.amountAndUse: Acidity is measured as pH. A percentage without pH and use directions is not enough to compare strength. A brief rinse-off product, a leave-on lotion and a peel need their own product context.
glycolic-acid.distinctIngredients: Glycolate salts and esters are distinct ingredients. AHA names a family, not this exact ingredient.

lactic-acid.name: Lactic Acid
lactic-acid.summary: Holds moisture and can help surface skin shed
lactic-acid.body: Lactic acid can help hold moisture and, in an exfoliating formula, smooth the skin’s surface. It can also adjust a product’s acidity.
lactic-acid.detail: Like glycolic acid, it belongs to the AHA family. Its presence alone does not make a product a peel: the amount, acidity and whole formula determine how much skin shedding to expect.
lactic-acid.evidence: The ingredient reference supports water holding and acidity control; FDA supports the AHA skin-shedding explanation.
lactic-acid.caution: Follow the AHA sun-protection guidance: sunscreen, protective clothing and limited sun exposure during use and for a week afterward. This is FDA’s AHA guidance, not a lactic-acid-specific trial result.
lactic-acid.amountAndUse: Percentage and pH both matter, along with whether the product is left on or rinsed off. Sodium lactate and sodium lauroyl lactylate are different ingredients, even though their names sound related.
lactic-acid.aliasNotes: 2-Hydroxypropanoic acid. Preserve any explicitly stated D or L form rather than guessing it from an unqualified label.
lactic-acid.distinctIngredients: Sodium lactate, ammonium lactate, lactate esters and the already approved sodium lauroyl lactylate are separate identities.

azelaic-acid.name: Azelaic Acid
azelaic-acid.summary: Used in certain acne and rosacea medicines
azelaic-acid.body: Azelaic acid is the active ingredient in some acne and rosacea medicines. In cosmetics, it can also help adjust acidity.
azelaic-acid.detail: The checked AZELEX 20% cream label covers inflammatory acne. The FINACEA 15% gel label covers inflamed rosacea bumps; it does not establish a benefit for redness alone. These are uses of those medicines, not promises about every cosmetic with azelaic acid.
azelaic-acid.evidence: Cosmetic acidity control and medicine-specific treatment uses have separate sources. The exact medicine and condition matter.
azelaic-acid.caution: The FINACEA gel label describes burning or stinging and says persistent severe irritation needs stopping and appropriate care. Treat that as guidance for the identified medicine, not an estimated reaction rate for all azelaic products.
azelaic-acid.amountAndUse: Keep the percentage and product form together. A 10% cosmetic, a 15% medicinal gel and a 20% medicinal cream are not automatically interchangeable, and the larger number does not establish the best result.
azelaic-acid.distinctIngredients: Potassium azeloyl diglycinate and other azelaic derivatives are separate identities. Azelaic acid is not an AHA.

ascorbic-acid.name: Ascorbic Acid
ascorbic-acid.summary: Vitamin C that helps limit oxidation
ascorbic-acid.body: Ascorbic acid is a form of vitamin C used to help limit certain damaging chemical reactions, called oxidation. It also has skin-care uses.
ascorbic-acid.detail: In one six-month study, a 5% vitamin C cream improved assessed signs of sun-aged skin compared with its cream base. That finding belongs to the studied cream; it does not establish the result of every vitamin C serum.
ascorbic-acid.evidence: Antioxidant and skin-care functions are documented. The human study is abstract-level evidence for one preparation, with no general ideal percentage or product ranking inferred.
ascorbic-acid.amountAndUse: The amount, acidity and whether vitamin C stays stable all matter. This is an antioxidant acid, not an exfoliating AHA. Vitamin C derivatives need their own entries and evidence.
ascorbic-acid.aliasNotes: L-Ascorbic acid where that form is explicitly identified. “Vitamin C” alone can refer to other forms, so it is not an automatic exact match.
ascorbic-acid.distinctIngredients: Ascorbyl glucoside, sodium ascorbyl phosphate, magnesium ascorbyl phosphate, ascorbyl palmitate and 3-O-ethyl ascorbic acid are separate ingredients.

retinol.name: Retinol
retinol.summary: Vitamin A ingredient studied for fine wrinkles
retinol.body: Retinol is a vitamin A ingredient used in skincare for fine lines and texture. Some studied creams improved fine wrinkles over several months.
retinol.detail: In a 26-week study of 57 middle-aged Japanese women, a nightly 0.075% retinol cream improved facial wrinkles more than its cream base. This is evidence about that preparation and population, not a guarantee for any current serum.
retinol.evidence: A controlled human study supports a fine-wrinkle benefit for a particular retinol cream. No universal concentration ranking or prescription substitution is inferred.
retinol.caution: Retinol products can irritate skin: three participants left that study because of irritation. AAD guidance favors gradual introduction, moisturizing and daytime sun protection rather than pushing through irritation. AAD also advises avoiding retinoids during pregnancy.
retinol.amountAndUse: Retinol is different from retinal and prescription tretinoin. The same percentage does not mean equivalent strength across them. Formula stability, packaging and use also matter; the study percentage is not a recommended starting dose.
retinol.aliasNotes: Vitamin A1; vitamin A alcohol. Generic “vitamin A” or “retinoid” is too broad for an exact match.
retinol.distinctIngredients: Retinal, retinyl esters, tretinoin/retinoic acid, adapalene and isotretinoin remain separate identities.

retinal.name: Retinal
retinal.summary: Vitamin A ingredient studied in texture care
retinal.body: Retinal, also called retinaldehyde, is a vitamin A ingredient used in cosmetic skincare. Research has tested particular creams for changes in skin texture.
retinal.detail: A three-month study of 40 Korean women compared 0.05% and 0.1% creams. Both groups improved in texture and hydration, with no significant difference between them on those measures; the inspected abstract describes no cream-base-only comparison.
retinal.evidence: The research supports formula-specific education. The 2026 study compared different formulas; the 2018 abstract describes no cream-base-only group. These limits prevent stronger ingredient or concentration claims.
retinal.caution: Irritation is possible with retinal products. A separate 2026 formula study had one withdrawal for redness and discomfort; its multi-ingredient formulas do not isolate retinal as the cause or establish a general reaction rate. AAD’s general guidance also advises avoiding retinoids during pregnancy.
retinal.amountAndUse: Retinal is distinct from retinol and tretinoin. Its chemical relationship to them does not establish a conversion ratio for product strength. A higher percentage alone is not proof of a better cream.
retinal.distinctIngredients: Retinol, retinyl esters and tretinoin/retinoic acid are different ingredients. Retinol-only safety assessments must not be applied to retinal by name similarity.

acetyl-glutamine.name: Acetyl Glutamine
acetyl-glutamine.summary: Helps maintain the skin’s feel and condition
acetyl-glutamine.body: Acetyl glutamine is a modified form of the amino acid glutamine used to help keep skin in good condition. It has a supporting role in a skin-care formula.
acetyl-glutamine.detail: The acetyl part of its name describes a small chemical group attached to glutamine.
acetyl-glutamine.aliasNotes: Acetylated glutamine; keep separate from glutamine and acetyl glutamic acid.
acetyl-glutamine.distinctIngredients: Acetylated glutamine; keep separate from glutamine and acetyl glutamic acid.

alanine.name: Alanine
alanine.summary: Helps hydrate skin as an amino-acid helper
alanine.body: Alanine is an amino acid that helps hydrate skin. In a cream or serum, it can contribute to the moisturizing blend that helps skin feel less dry.
alanine.detail: Amino acids are small building blocks of proteins, including structural proteins found in skin.
alanine.aliasNotes: Alanine is the individual amino acid, rather than a peptide or protein blend.

alpha-glucan-oligosaccharide.name: Alpha-Glucan Oligosaccharide
alpha-glucan-oligosaccharide.summary: Sugar-based helper for a smoother skin feel
alpha-glucan-oligosaccharide.body: Alpha-glucan oligosaccharide is made from short chains of sugar units. It is used to help condition skin and leave it feeling smoother.
alpha-glucan-oligosaccharide.detail: It is often discussed as a prebiotic ingredient, referring to its potential interaction with microorganisms on skin. That is a different question from its straightforward skin-conditioning role.
alpha-glucan-oligosaccharide.evidence: The page’s selective-microbe claims are supplier-attributed; this card does not promise a changed skin microbiome.
alpha-glucan-oligosaccharide.aliasNotes: An alpha-linked glucose oligomer; this name does not mean beta-glucan.
alpha-glucan-oligosaccharide.distinctIngredients: An alpha-linked glucose oligomer; this name does not mean beta-glucan.

arginine.name: Arginine
arginine.summary: Amino-acid helper for keeping skin hydrated
arginine.body: Arginine is an amino acid found among the substances that help skin hold moisture. In skin care, it can support hydration and contribute to a comfortable skin feel.
arginine.aliasNotes: Individual arginine amino acid, not a peptide complex.

aspartic-acid.name: Aspartic Acid
aspartic-acid.summary: Helps hydrate skin and control product acidity
aspartic-acid.body: Aspartic acid is an amino acid that can help hydrate skin. It can also help a formula maintain its intended acidity, which affects how the other ingredients behave.
aspartic-acid.detail: This acidity-control job is called buffering. The word acid in the name does not, by itself, mean the ingredient is being used as an exfoliant.
aspartic-acid.aliasNotes: Aspartic acid is kept separate from its salts and from other amino acids.
aspartic-acid.distinctIngredients: Aspartic acid is kept separate from its salts and from other amino acids.

beta-glucan.name: Beta-Glucan
beta-glucan.summary: Sugar-chain ingredient that helps keep skin hydrated
beta-glucan.body: Beta-glucan is a large molecule made from linked sugar units. In skin care, it helps moisturize skin and can be part of a formula designed for a more comfortable feel.
beta-glucan.detail: Beta-glucans occur in sources such as yeast and cereals. Their structure and source can differ, so the ingredient name alone does not describe a particular tested preparation.
beta-glucan.aliasNotes: Beta-linked glucose polymer; not alpha-glucan oligosaccharide.
beta-glucan.distinctIngredients: Beta-linked glucose polymer; not alpha-glucan oligosaccharide.

betaine.name: Betaine
betaine.summary: Water-binding helper that also improves product feel
betaine.body: Betaine helps hold water and contributes to skin hydration. It can also improve how a formula feels, making it a useful supporting ingredient in moisturizers and cleansers.
betaine.detail: It belongs to a group called osmolytes: small substances involved in balancing water around cells. Cosmetic betaine is an amino-acid derivative and may be obtained from sugar beet.
betaine.aliasNotes: Betaine itself is the subject of this card; ingredients with longer betaine names are not automatically the same substance.
betaine.distinctIngredients: Betaine itself is the subject of this card; ingredients with longer betaine names are not automatically the same substance.

cysteine.name: Cysteine
cysteine.summary: Helps protect formula ingredients from oxidative change
cysteine.body: Cysteine can act as an antioxidant, helping limit chemical changes caused by oxygen in a formula. It also has uses in hair conditioning and in products that reshape hair.
cysteine.aliasNotes: The free cysteine ingredient is kept separate from cysteine hydrochloride and acetyl cysteine.
cysteine.distinctIngredients: The free cysteine ingredient is kept separate from cysteine hydrochloride and acetyl cysteine.

diglycerin.name: Diglycerin
diglycerin.summary: Helps bind water to keep skin hydrated
diglycerin.body: Diglycerin is a water-binding moisturizer made from two connected glycerin units. It helps keep moisture in the upper layers of skin, supporting a less dry feel.
diglycerin.detail: The larger structure makes it a distinct ingredient from glycerin. Formulators can use it alongside other water-binding ingredients to build the texture and moisturizing character of a product.
diglycerin.aliasNotes: A glycerin dimer, kept separate from glycerin and longer polyglycerins.
diglycerin.distinctIngredients: A glycerin dimer, kept separate from glycerin and longer polyglycerins.

fructooligosaccharides.name: Fructooligosaccharides
fructooligosaccharides.summary: Sugar-chain helper that holds moisture in formulas
fructooligosaccharides.body: Fructooligosaccharides are short chains of sugar units used to hold moisture in cosmetic products. They also help condition skin as part of a moisturizing formula.
fructooligosaccharides.detail: The long name refers to a group of related carbohydrates, rather than a single simple sugar.
fructooligosaccharides.aliasNotes: Oligosaccharide mixture chiefly described as kestose, nystose and fructosyl nystose; not equivalent to fructose alone.
fructooligosaccharides.distinctIngredients: Oligosaccharide mixture chiefly described as kestose, nystose and fructosyl nystose; not equivalent to fructose alone.

fructose.name: Fructose
fructose.summary: A simple sugar that helps bind water
fructose.body: Fructose, also known as fruit sugar, helps keep skin hydrated by binding water. In a cosmetic formula it is a moisture-supporting helper.
fructose.detail: This type of water-binding ingredient is called a humectant. It can contribute to a moisturizer’s overall feel alongside oils, texture helpers and other ingredients.
fructose.aliasNotes: Individual fructose sugar; separate from fructooligosaccharides.

glucose.name: Glucose
glucose.summary: Water-binding sugar that supports skin hydration
glucose.body: Glucose is a simple sugar that helps bind water in skin-care formulas. That makes it a useful supporting ingredient for keeping skin hydrated.
glucose.detail: Its water-binding job is called humectancy. It can work alongside other moisturizing ingredients to support a formula’s overall hydrating feel.
glucose.aliasNotes: Individual glucose sugar; not a generic name for all sugars.

glutamic-acid.name: Glutamic Acid
glutamic-acid.summary: Helps hold water and adjust product acidity
glutamic-acid.body: Glutamic acid is an amino acid that helps hold water in a skin-care formula. It can also help adjust the product’s acidity, supporting the conditions the formula needs.
glutamic-acid.detail: It is a small individual molecule. Polyglutamic acid is a different ingredient made from linked glutamic-acid units, so their names and evidence should not be used interchangeably.
glutamic-acid.aliasNotes: Glutamic acid is separate from polyglutamic acid, glutamine and acetyl glutamine.
glutamic-acid.distinctIngredients: Glutamic acid is separate from polyglutamic acid, glutamine and acetyl glutamine.

glycine.name: Glycine
glycine.summary: Amino-acid ingredient that contributes to skin hydration
glycine.body: Glycine is an amino acid used as a moisturizing ingredient in skin care. It can be one of several small water-friendly ingredients that help skin feel less dry.
glycine.detail: Glycine is also part of many proteins and peptides. Free glycine in an ingredient list is a different material from a named peptide that includes glycine within its structure.
glycine.aliasNotes: The free amino acid glycine, rather than a glycine-containing peptide.
glycine.distinctIngredients: The free amino acid glycine, rather than a glycine-containing peptide.

histidine.name: Histidine
histidine.summary: Amino-acid helper that holds onto water
histidine.body: Histidine is an amino acid that helps retain moisture and condition skin. In a moisturizer or serum, it can contribute to a less dry feel.
histidine.detail: The term humectant describes this water-holding job.

hydrolyzed-collagen.name: Hydrolyzed Collagen
hydrolyzed-collagen.summary: Broken-down protein that binds water and softens skin
hydrolyzed-collagen.body: Hydrolyzed collagen is collagen broken into smaller protein fragments. It helps skin hold moisture and feel smoother, giving it a useful role in creams, serums and other cosmetics.
hydrolyzed-collagen.detail: Hydrolyzed describes that breakdown process. The result is a mixture of fragments, so it should not be confused with replacing the intact collagen that gives skin its structure.
hydrolyzed-collagen.evidence: Source and fragment sizes can vary between raw materials; the ingredient name does not supply those details.
hydrolyzed-collagen.aliasNotes: Collagen hydrolysate, distinct from intact or soluble collagen.
hydrolyzed-collagen.distinctIngredients: Collagen hydrolysate, distinct from intact or soluble collagen.

hydrolyzed-rice-protein.name: Hydrolyzed Rice Protein
hydrolyzed-rice-protein.summary: Rice-protein fragments that help condition skin
hydrolyzed-rice-protein.body: Hydrolyzed rice protein is rice protein broken into smaller pieces and used to help condition skin. It can also help improve softness and manageability in hair products.
hydrolyzed-rice-protein.detail: The breakdown process produces a mixture of amino acids and protein fragments. This is a more specific ingredient than rice water or a general rice extract.
hydrolyzed-rice-protein.aliasNotes: Rice protein hydrolysate, separate from rice extract, rice water and modified rice-protein derivatives.
hydrolyzed-rice-protein.distinctIngredients: Rice protein hydrolysate, separate from rice extract, rice water and modified rice-protein derivatives.

hydrolyzed-sodium-hyaluronate.name: Hydrolyzed Sodium Hyaluronate
hydrolyzed-sodium-hyaluronate.summary: Smaller hyaluronate fragments that help retain moisture
hydrolyzed-sodium-hyaluronate.body: Hydrolyzed sodium hyaluronate is a broken-down form of sodium hyaluronate used to help moisturize skin. The shorter fragments give formulators another form of this water-binding ingredient to work with.
hydrolyzed-sodium-hyaluronate.amountAndUse: The name alone does not specify the size of the fragments; that depends on the raw material.
hydrolyzed-sodium-hyaluronate.aliasNotes: Hydrolysate of sodium hyaluronate; separate from sodium hyaluronate, hyaluronic acid and sodium hyaluronate crosspolymer.
hydrolyzed-sodium-hyaluronate.distinctIngredients: Hydrolysate of sodium hyaluronate; separate from sodium hyaluronate, hyaluronic acid and sodium hyaluronate crosspolymer.

hydrolyzed-yeast-protein.name: Hydrolyzed Yeast Protein
hydrolyzed-yeast-protein.summary: Yeast-protein fragments used to help condition skin
hydrolyzed-yeast-protein.body: Hydrolyzed yeast protein is protein from yeast broken into smaller pieces. It is used to help condition skin and can also help hair feel softer and easier to manage.
hydrolyzed-yeast-protein.detail: The ingredient is a processed protein mixture, not simply live yeast added to a product. Hydrolyzed tells you about the breakdown process rather than a particular skin-treatment benefit.
hydrolyzed-yeast-protein.aliasNotes: Protein hydrolysate from Saccharomyces cerevisiae; separate from yeast extract and general yeast ferment ingredients.
hydrolyzed-yeast-protein.distinctIngredients: Protein hydrolysate from Saccharomyces cerevisiae; separate from yeast extract and general yeast ferment ingredients.

isoleucine.name: Isoleucine
isoleucine.summary: Amino-acid helper that contributes to skin moisture
isoleucine.body: Isoleucine is an amino acid used to help moisturize and condition skin. It can be part of an amino-acid blend that supports a skin-care formula’s moisturizing feel.
isoleucine.detail: It has a related name to leucine but is a distinct ingredient. Keep those identities separate when comparing formulas or reading about a particular tested blend.
isoleucine.aliasNotes: Individual isoleucine amino acid; separate from leucine.
isoleucine.distinctIngredients: Individual isoleucine amino acid; separate from leucine.

isomalt.name: Isomalt
isomalt.summary: Sugar-derived helper that holds moisture in products
isomalt.body: Isomalt is a sugar-derived ingredient used to hold moisture in cosmetic products. It is a humectant, meaning it helps keep water in the formula.
isomalt.detail: It is made by processing sucrose with enzymes. The resulting mixture has its own ingredient identity, separate from the starting sugar.
isomalt.aliasNotes: A sucrose-derived mixture identified under the INCI name isomalt.
isomalt.distinctIngredients: A sucrose-derived mixture identified under the INCI name isomalt.

leucine.name: Leucine
leucine.summary: Amino-acid helper for skin and hair condition
leucine.body: Leucine is an amino acid used to help condition skin and hair. In hair products it can contribute to a softer, more manageable feel.

sources.label: Safety Assessment of α-Amino Acids as Used in Cosmetics, final report 2012

lysine.name: Lysine
lysine.summary: Amino-acid ingredient used to help condition skin
lysine.body: Lysine is an amino acid used to help condition skin and hair. This means helping maintain their feel and overall condition.
lysine.aliasNotes: The free lysine amino acid, separate from lysine hydrochloride and acylated lysine derivatives.
lysine.distinctIngredients: The free lysine amino acid, separate from lysine hydrochloride and acylated lysine derivatives.

sources.label: Safety Assessment of α-Amino Acids as Used in Cosmetics, final report 2012

maltodextrin.name: Maltodextrin
maltodextrin.summary: Helps hold formulas together and manage texture
maltodextrin.body: Maltodextrin is a starch-derived helper that can bind ingredients together and help an oil-and-water mixture stay uniform. It can also absorb material at the surface, contributing to a more matte feel.
maltodextrin.detail: Its job is often behind the scenes: supporting the product’s structure and finish. Corn, rice and potato starch are possible starting materials.
maltodextrin.aliasNotes: Starch-derived maltodextrin; separate from the simple sugar maltose.
maltodextrin.distinctIngredients: Starch-derived maltodextrin; separate from the simple sugar maltose.

maltose.name: Maltose
maltose.summary: Sugar ingredient that helps skin stay soft
maltose.body: Maltose is a sugar used to help moisturize and condition skin. It contributes to keeping skin soft and smooth as part of the finished formula.
maltose.detail: It is also known as malt sugar. That name identifies the sugar itself, which should be kept separate from maltodextrin when comparing ingredient lists.
maltose.aliasNotes: Maltose, also called malt sugar; distinct from maltodextrin.
maltose.distinctIngredients: Maltose, also called malt sugar; distinct from maltodextrin.

mannitol.name: Mannitol
mannitol.summary: Water-binding ingredient that supports skin hydration
mannitol.body: Mannitol helps bind water and keep skin hydrated. It is used as a moisture-supporting helper and can also help hold a cosmetic product together.
mannitol.detail: The moisture-retention role is called humectancy; the hold-together role is called binding. A single ingredient can perform both jobs depending on the formula.
mannitol.aliasNotes: Mannitol is kept separate from the similarly named sugar mannose.

mannose.name: Mannose
mannose.summary: Simple sugar that helps a formula hold water
mannose.body: Mannose is a sugar used to help retain moisture in skin-care products. It supports hydration as part of the formula’s blend of water-binding ingredients.
mannose.detail: Its ingredient function is called humectancy. This is a straightforward supporting role in a formula, alongside ingredients chosen for softness and texture.
mannose.aliasNotes: Individual mannose sugar; distinct from mannitol.

pca.name: PCA
pca.summary: Helps skin hold onto its natural moisture
pca.body: PCA helps skin hold water and stay hydrated. It is one of the small moisture-binding substances naturally present in skin and is also used in cosmetic formulas.
pca.detail: The letters stand for pyrrolidone carboxylic acid. This belongs to skin’s natural moisturizing factor, a mixture of water-holding substances in its outer layer.
pca.aliasNotes: Pyrrolidone carboxylic acid itself; separate from sodium PCA and other PCA salts.
pca.distinctIngredients: Pyrrolidone carboxylic acid itself; separate from sodium PCA and other PCA salts.

phenylalanine.name: Phenylalanine
phenylalanine.summary: Amino-acid helper used for skin conditioning
phenylalanine.body: Phenylalanine is an amino acid used to help condition skin and hair. In a cosmetic, that is a supporting role concerned with their feel and condition.

sources.label: Safety Assessment of α-Amino Acids as Used in Cosmetics, final report 2012

proline.name: Proline
proline.summary: Amino-acid helper that helps condition skin
proline.body: Proline is an amino acid used as a skin- and hair-conditioning ingredient. Its practical cosmetic role is to help maintain their feel and condition.
proline.aliasNotes: Individual proline amino acid; separate from proline-containing peptides.
proline.distinctIngredients: Individual proline amino acid; separate from proline-containing peptides.

sources.label: Safety Assessment of α-Amino Acids as Used in Cosmetics, final report 2012

rhamnose.name: Rhamnose
rhamnose.summary: Water-binding helper used to support skin hydration
rhamnose.body: Rhamnose helps retain moisture and can contribute to a moisturizing skin-care formula. It is a supporting water-binding ingredient, also called a humectant.
rhamnose.aliasNotes: Rhamnose is identified as 6-deoxy-L-mannose; keep separate from mannose.
rhamnose.distinctIngredients: Rhamnose is identified as 6-deoxy-L-mannose; keep separate from mannose.

sources.label: AC-Rhamnose – SOHO ANECO Chemicals technical datasheet on SpecialChem

serine.name: Serine
serine.summary: Amino acid that helps hold water in skin
serine.body: Serine is an amino acid that binds water and helps support skin hydration. It often joins other moisturizing ingredients in a formula rather than working on its own.
serine.detail: A moisturizing complex is simply a blend of ingredients chosen to work together. Serine supplies one of the small water-binding components in that blend.

sodium-hyaluronate-crosspolymer.name: Sodium Hyaluronate Crosspolymer
sodium-hyaluronate-crosspolymer.summary: Linked hyaluronate network that holds water on skin
sodium-hyaluronate-crosspolymer.body: Sodium hyaluronate crosspolymer helps hold water and forms a smooth film on skin. It is made by linking hyaluronate chains together into a larger network.
sodium-hyaluronate-crosspolymer.detail: Crosspolymer describes those connections between chains. This structure gives the ingredient a different texture and form from ordinary sodium hyaluronate while keeping a moisture-supporting role.
sodium-hyaluronate-crosspolymer.aliasNotes: Crosslinked sodium hyaluronate; distinct from sodium hyaluronate and hydrolyzed sodium hyaluronate.
sodium-hyaluronate-crosspolymer.distinctIngredients: Crosslinked sodium hyaluronate; distinct from sodium hyaluronate and hydrolyzed sodium hyaluronate.

sodium-lactate.name: Sodium Lactate
sodium-lactate.summary: Helps hold moisture and control product acidity
sodium-lactate.body: Sodium lactate helps keep skin hydrated and can help a formula maintain its intended acidity. It is the sodium salt form of lactic acid.
sodium-lactate.detail: The acidity-control role is called buffering. Moisture support and pH control are both useful formulation jobs, and the balance depends on how the ingredient is used.
sodium-lactate.aliasNotes: Sodium salt of lactic acid, kept separate from free lactic acid.
sodium-lactate.distinctIngredients: Sodium salt of lactic acid, kept separate from free lactic acid.

sodium-pca.name: Sodium PCA
sodium-pca.summary: Water-binding ingredient that supports skin’s moisture balance
sodium-pca.body: Sodium PCA helps skin hold onto water and stay hydrated. It is the sodium salt of PCA, a substance found naturally among skin’s moisture-binding components.
sodium-pca.detail: PCA is short for pyrrolidone carboxylic acid. Sodium PCA is a distinct salt form, so its name is recorded separately from PCA and from other salts such as zinc PCA.
sodium-pca.aliasNotes: Sodium salt of pyrrolidone carboxylic acid; distinct from PCA and other PCA salts.
sodium-pca.distinctIngredients: Sodium salt of pyrrolidone carboxylic acid; distinct from PCA and other PCA salts.

sorbitol.name: Sorbitol
sorbitol.summary: Helps hold water and improve a product’s glide
sorbitol.body: Sorbitol helps skin hold water and contributes to a moisturizing feel. It can also give a formula more body and slip, helping it spread smoothly.
sorbitol.detail: Those texture effects explain why a water-binding ingredient may be useful in more than just a moisturizer. Its final feel depends on the rest of the formula.
sorbitol.aliasNotes: Sorbitol is identified chemically as D-glucitol.

threonine.name: Threonine
threonine.summary: Amino-acid helper that contributes to skin hydration
threonine.body: Threonine is an amino acid used to help hydrate skin. It can contribute to a formula’s moisturizing blend and the less dry feel that blend is designed to provide.

trehalose.name: Trehalose
trehalose.summary: Sugar ingredient that helps keep skin hydrated
trehalose.body: Trehalose is a sugar that helps bind water and keep skin hydrated. It can be one of several ingredients contributing to the moisturizing feel of a cream or serum.
trehalose.detail: Its water-binding function is called humectancy. This makes trehalose a practical helper for formulas designed to maintain moisture.
trehalose.aliasNotes: Individual trehalose sugar; separate from other sugars such as glucose and maltose.

tyrosine.name: Tyrosine
tyrosine.summary: Amino-acid ingredient used to help condition skin
tyrosine.body: Tyrosine is an amino acid used to help condition skin and hair. Its cosmetic role is to support their feel and condition within a formula.
tyrosine.aliasNotes: Individual tyrosine amino acid; distinct from acetyl tyrosine and other tyrosine derivatives.
tyrosine.distinctIngredients: Individual tyrosine amino acid; distinct from acetyl tyrosine and other tyrosine derivatives.

sources.label: Safety Assessment of α-Amino Acids as Used in Cosmetics, final report 2012

valine.name: Valine
valine.summary: Amino-acid helper for skin and hair condition
valine.body: Valine is an amino acid used in skin- and hair-conditioning formulas. It has a supporting role in maintaining the feel and condition of skin or hair.

sources.label: Safety Assessment of α-Amino Acids as Used in Cosmetics, final report 2012

xylitol.name: Xylitol
xylitol.summary: Water-binding helper that supports a moisturizing formula
xylitol.body: Xylitol helps hold moisture and condition skin. It can contribute to a formula’s hydrating feel, including when used alongside other water-binding ingredients.
xylitol.detail: Some raw-material blends combine xylitol with other ingredients. The name xylitol identifies this component, so a blend’s full results should stay associated with the blend.
xylitol.aliasNotes: Individual xylitol ingredient; not synonymous with the Aquaxyl trade blend or xylitylglucoside.
xylitol.distinctIngredients: Individual xylitol ingredient; not synonymous with the Aquaxyl trade blend or xylitylglucoside.

astrocaryum-murumuru-seed-butter.name: Astrocaryum Murumuru Seed Butter
astrocaryum-murumuru-seed-butter.summary: Softens skin with a rich plant butter.
astrocaryum-murumuru-seed-butter.body: Murumuru seed butter is a plant fat that helps skin feel softer and smoother. It brings a buttery component to moisturizers and balms.
astrocaryum-murumuru-seed-butter.aliasNotes: Fat obtained from Astrocaryum murumuru seeds.

sources.label: ASTROCARYUM MURUMURU SEED BUTTER — COSMILE Europe

beeswax.name: Beeswax
beeswax.summary: Softens skin and gives balms their body.
beeswax.body: Beeswax helps soften skin while thickening a formula. Its solid, waxy texture is useful when a balm or cream needs more body.
beeswax.aliasNotes: Wax obtained from honeycomb; INKEEDecoder identifies Beeswax under Cera Alba.

behenic-acid.name: Behenic Acid
behenic-acid.summary: Helps oil and water mix in formulas.
behenic-acid.body: Behenic acid helps a formula combine oil and water, and can make it look more opaque. In cleansing products, it can also contribute to washing away oils and dirt.
behenic-acid.aliasNotes: Behenic acid is docosanoic acid, a long-chain fatty acid.

butylene-glycol-cocoate.name: Butylene Glycol Cocoate
butylene-glycol-cocoate.summary: Keeps oil and water blended evenly.
butylene-glycol-cocoate.body: Butylene glycol cocoate helps oil and water stay mixed in creams and lotions. It also helps adjust how thick or fluid a product feels.
butylene-glycol-cocoate.aliasNotes: An ester made with butylene glycol and coconut-oil fatty acids.
butylene-glycol-cocoate.distinctIngredients: Distinct from butylene glycol alone and from coconut oil.

butyloctyl-salicylate.name: Butyloctyl Salicylate
butyloctyl-salicylate.summary: Helps ingredients dissolve and products spread smoothly.
butyloctyl-salicylate.body: Butyloctyl salicylate helps dissolve other ingredients and gives products a smooth, easy-spreading feel. It is often used as a formulation helper in sunscreens.
butyloctyl-salicylate.distinctIngredients: A separate ingredient from salicylic acid; do not substitute salicylic-acid exfoliation claims.

butyrospermum-parkii-shea-butter.name: Butyrospermum Parkii (Shea) Butter
butyrospermum-parkii-shea-butter.summary: Adds richness and helps skin feel softer.
butyrospermum-parkii-shea-butter.body: Shea Butter is a plant fat that gives creams and balms a rich, softening feel. It helps smooth dry-feeling skin and contributes body to the product’s texture.
butyrospermum-parkii-shea-butter.detail: The ingredient is the butter obtained from the shea tree, rather than a general leaf or bark extract. Its rich feel can vary with how much is used and what it is blended with.
butyrospermum-parkii-shea-butter.aliasNotes: Butyrospermum Parkii (Shea) Butter matches the opened Butyrospermum Parkii Butter record, whose alias is Shea Butter.

c12-15-alkyl-benzoate.name: C12-15 Alkyl Benzoate
c12-15-alkyl-benzoate.summary: Softens skin and improves a product’s glide.
c12-15-alkyl-benzoate.body: C12-15 alkyl benzoate helps skin feel smooth without adding a heavy, waxy texture. It also helps dissolve oil-soluble ingredients, which makes it useful in sunscreen formulas.
c12-15-alkyl-benzoate.aliasNotes: A mixture of benzoic-acid esters with C12–15 alcohol chains.

c12-16-alcohols.name: C12-16 Alcohols
c12-16-alcohols.summary: Softens skin and helps creams hold together.
c12-16-alcohols.body: C12-16 alcohols are a mixture of long-chain, fatty alcohols that soften skin. They also help control a cream’s thickness and keep its oil and water parts evenly mixed.
c12-16-alcohols.aliasNotes: Alcohol mixture with carbon chains ranging from 12 to 16 atoms.
c12-16-alcohols.distinctIngredients: This fatty-alcohol mixture is different from ethanol, often listed simply as Alcohol.

c13-15-alkane.name: C13-15 Alkane
c13-15-alkane.summary: Adds glide with a light after-feel.
c13-15-alkane.body: C13-15 alkane helps a product spread smoothly and leaves a light, less oily feel. It can also act as a solvent, helping other ingredients dissolve into the formula.
c13-15-alkane.aliasNotes: A mixture of alkanes with 13–15 carbon atoms.

caprooyl-phytosphingosine.name: Caprooyl Phytosphingosine
caprooyl-phytosphingosine.summary: Helps keep skin in good condition.
caprooyl-phytosphingosine.body: Caprooyl phytosphingosine is a fat-related ingredient used to help maintain skin’s condition. It is made by joining phytosphingosine to caproic acid, a fatty acid.
caprooyl-phytosphingosine.distinctIngredients: Keep separate from free phytosphingosine and from caprooyl sphingosine.

caprooyl-sphingosine.name: Caprooyl Sphingosine
caprooyl-sphingosine.summary: Helps keep skin in good condition.
caprooyl-sphingosine.body: Caprooyl sphingosine is a fat-related skin-conditioning ingredient. Joining sphingosine to caproic acid creates this distinct ingredient for use in skin-care formulas.
caprooyl-sphingosine.distinctIngredients: Keep separate from free sphingosine and from caprooyl phytosphingosine.

caprylyl-caprylate-caprate.name: Caprylyl Caprylate/Caprate
caprylyl-caprylate-caprate.summary: Softens skin with a light, dry finish.
caprylyl-caprylate-caprate.body: Caprylyl caprylate/caprate helps a product glide across skin and leaves it feeling smooth. It is a liquid skin softener that can make an oily formula feel lighter.
caprylyl-caprylate-caprate.aliasNotes: Caprylyl alcohol esterified with a mixture of caprylic and capric acids.
caprylyl-caprylate-caprate.distinctIngredients: Different from caprylic/capric triglyceride and from coco-caprylate/caprate.

carthamus-tinctorius-safflower-seed-oil.name: Carthamus Tinctorius (Safflower) Seed Oil
carthamus-tinctorius-safflower-seed-oil.summary: Softens skin with safflower seed oil.
carthamus-tinctorius-safflower-seed-oil.body: Safflower seed oil helps smooth and soften skin, adding an oily component to moisturizers. Its fatty-acid makeup includes linoleic and oleic acids.
carthamus-tinctorius-safflower-seed-oil.amountAndUse: The balance of fatty acids can differ between oil varieties and preparations.
carthamus-tinctorius-safflower-seed-oil.aliasNotes: Fixed oil from Carthamus tinctorius seeds.
carthamus-tinctorius-safflower-seed-oil.distinctIngredients: Separate from safflower flower extracts or isolated linoleic acid.

ceramide-eos.name: Ceramide EOS
ceramide-eos.summary: Adds a ceramide fat to moisturizing formulas.
ceramide-eos.body: Ceramide EOS is a type of ceramide, a fat used to help keep skin in good condition. Ceramides belong to the family of fats that make up skin’s outer protective layer.
ceramide-eos.detail: In moisturizers, ceramides are commonly combined with other fats and moisturizing ingredients. The whole formula matters to how well the product helps skin hold moisture.
ceramide-eos.aliasNotes: EOS identifies a sphingosine-based ceramide linked to an esterified omega-hydroxy fatty acid.
ceramide-eos.distinctIngredients: Keep separate from Ceramide EOP, NP, NS and other named ceramides.

ceramide-ns.name: Ceramide NS
ceramide-ns.summary: Adds a ceramide fat to moisturizing formulas.
ceramide-ns.body: Ceramide NS is a skin-conditioning fat in the ceramide family. Ceramides are part of skin’s outer protective layer and are used in moisturizers to support soft, moisturized skin.
ceramide-ns.aliasNotes: NS denotes sphingosine joined to a normal, non-hydroxy fatty acid; the older Ceramide 2 category had a broader scope.
ceramide-ns.distinctIngredients: Do not merge with Ceramide NG or treat every ingredient formerly called Ceramide 2 as identical to Ceramide NS.

cetearyl-isononanoate.name: Cetearyl Isononanoate
cetearyl-isononanoate.summary: Softens skin and adds slip to creams.
cetearyl-isononanoate.body: Cetearyl isononanoate is an oily ingredient that helps skin feel softer and smoother. It gives creams and lotions a more easily spreadable feel.
cetearyl-isononanoate.aliasNotes: Esters of isononanoic acid with C16–18 fatty alcohols.
cetearyl-isononanoate.distinctIngredients: A separate ingredient from cetearyl alcohol.

cetyl-alcohol.name: Cetyl Alcohol
cetyl-alcohol.summary: Softens skin and gives creams more body.
cetyl-alcohol.body: Cetyl alcohol is a waxy fatty alcohol that helps skin feel smooth. It also thickens creams and helps keep their oil and water parts blended.
cetyl-alcohol.aliasNotes: Cetyl alcohol is hexadecan-1-ol, a 16-carbon fatty alcohol.
cetyl-alcohol.distinctIngredients: Different from ethanol and from the cetearyl-alcohol mixture.

cetyl-lactate.name: Cetyl Lactate
cetyl-lactate.summary: Adds slip and a smooth skin feel.
cetyl-lactate.body: Cetyl lactate helps products glide over skin and leaves a smooth, silky feel. It is used as a skin-softening ingredient in the oily part of a formula.
cetyl-lactate.aliasNotes: Cetyl lactate is hexadecyl 2-hydroxypropanoate, an ester of cetyl alcohol and lactic acid.
cetyl-lactate.distinctIngredients: Separate from lactic acid; do not transfer exfoliating-acid claims to this ester.

cetyl-palmitate.name: Cetyl Palmitate
cetyl-palmitate.summary: Softens skin and thickens the product texture.
cetyl-palmitate.body: Cetyl palmitate is a waxy ingredient that makes skin feel softer. It also adds body to creams and balms, helping create a richer texture.
cetyl-palmitate.aliasNotes: The ester of cetyl alcohol and palmitic acid.
cetyl-palmitate.distinctIngredients: Separate from cetyl alcohol and palmitic acid as individual ingredients.

coco-caprylate-caprate.name: Coco-Caprylate/Caprate
coco-caprylate-caprate.summary: Softens skin with a silky, light finish.
coco-caprylate-caprate.body: Coco-caprylate/caprate helps a formula spread easily and leaves skin feeling smooth. It is useful when a product needs an oily skin-softening ingredient with a relatively light finish.
coco-caprylate-caprate.aliasNotes: Mixed caprylic/capric-acid esters of coconut-derived fatty alcohols.
coco-caprylate-caprate.distinctIngredients: Separate from coconut oil, caprylyl caprylate/caprate and caprylic/capric triglyceride.

coconut-alkanes.name: Coconut Alkanes
coconut-alkanes.summary: Adds glide and a light skin feel.
coconut-alkanes.body: Coconut alkanes are a light liquid that helps products spread and skin feel smooth. Some of the liquid evaporates after application, which helps reduce a lingering oily feel.
coconut-alkanes.aliasNotes: Hydrocarbons produced by reducing and hydrogenating coconut-oil fatty acids.
coconut-alkanes.distinctIngredients: A processed derivative rather than coconut oil itself; it is also separate from coco-caprylate/caprate.

dicaprylyl-carbonate.name: Dicaprylyl Carbonate
dicaprylyl-carbonate.summary: Softens skin with a dry, velvety feel.
dicaprylyl-carbonate.body: Dicaprylyl carbonate helps products spread easily and leaves skin feeling smooth. It can also dissolve some sunscreen ingredients, helping the formula feel lighter during application.
dicaprylyl-carbonate.aliasNotes: The dicaprylyl ester of carbonic acid.

dicaprylyl-ether.name: Dicaprylyl Ether
dicaprylyl-ether.summary: Adds smooth glide without a heavy finish.
dicaprylyl-ether.body: Dicaprylyl ether is an oily liquid that spreads quickly and softens skin. It can help give creams, lotions and oils a lighter-feeling finish.

ethyl-linoleate.name: Ethyl Linoleate
ethyl-linoleate.summary: Helps skin feel softer and smoother.
ethyl-linoleate.body: Ethyl linoleate is a modified form of linoleic acid used to soften and smooth skin. It is an ester, made by chemically joining the fatty acid with ethanol.
ethyl-linoleate.distinctIngredients: Different from free linoleic acid and from ethyl linolenate.

ethylhexyl-olivate.name: Ethylhexyl Olivate
ethylhexyl-olivate.summary: Helps keep skin in good condition.
ethylhexyl-olivate.body: Ethylhexyl olivate is a skin-conditioning ingredient made using fatty acids from olive oil. It is used in skin-care formulas as a processed fatty-acid ingredient.
ethylhexyl-olivate.distinctIngredients: Separate from olive fruit oil and from hydrogenated ethylhexyl olivate.

ethylhexyl-palmitate.name: Ethylhexyl Palmitate
ethylhexyl-palmitate.summary: Softens skin and adds richness to formulas.
ethylhexyl-palmitate.body: Ethylhexyl palmitate gives products a richer, smoother feel as they spread over skin. It is often blended with other skin-softening ingredients to shape the final texture.

euterpe-oleracea-sterols.name: Euterpe Oleracea Sterols
euterpe-oleracea-sterols.summary: Uses plant fats to help condition skin.
euterpe-oleracea-sterols.body: Euterpe oleracea sterols are a group of fat-like substances separated from the açaí palm. They are used to help keep skin in good condition.
euterpe-oleracea-sterols.aliasNotes: Sterol fraction isolated from Euterpe oleracea; the INCI description specifies the whole plant.
euterpe-oleracea-sterols.distinctIngredients: Separate from açaí fruit extract and açaí oil; berry antioxidant claims do not automatically apply.

glycolipids.name: Glycolipids
glycolipids.summary: Helps condition skin with sugar-linked fats.
glycolipids.body: Glycolipids are fats with sugar components attached to them. In skin-care formulas, they are used to help keep skin in good condition.
glycolipids.amountAndUse: This is a group name, so it does not identify one single molecule or a fixed mixture.
glycolipids.aliasNotes: Mixture of carbohydrate-linked lipids, meaning sugar-linked fats.
glycolipids.distinctIngredients: The broad Glycolipids name is not interchangeable with a specific ceramide or a named cleansing glycolipid.

glycosphingolipids.name: Glycosphingolipids
glycosphingolipids.summary: Helps keep skin feeling soft and smooth.
glycosphingolipids.body: Glycosphingolipids are a type of fat with sugar components attached. They are used in skin care to help condition the skin and support a soft, smooth feel.
glycosphingolipids.aliasNotes: Sugar-containing sphingolipids; a more specific group than glycolipids.
glycosphingolipids.distinctIngredients: Keep separate from the broader Glycolipids name and from individual ceramides.

gossypium-herbaceum-cotton-seed-oil.name: Gossypium Herbaceum (Cotton) Seed Oil
gossypium-herbaceum-cotton-seed-oil.summary: Adds cottonseed oil to help condition skin.
gossypium-herbaceum-cotton-seed-oil.body: Cottonseed oil is the fixed, fatty oil obtained from cotton seeds. It is used in skin-care products to help keep skin in good condition.
gossypium-herbaceum-cotton-seed-oil.aliasNotes: Gossypium herbaceum seed oil; INKEEDecoder’s registry description encompasses oil expressed from Gossypium seeds.
gossypium-herbaceum-cotton-seed-oil.distinctIngredients: Keep separate from cotton extracts and hydrogenated cottonseed oil.

sources.label: GOSSYPIUM HERBACEUM SEED OIL — COSMILE Europe

helianthus-annuus-sunflower-seed-oil.name: Helianthus Annuus (Sunflower) Seed Oil
helianthus-annuus-sunflower-seed-oil.summary: Softens skin and helps it hold moisture.
helianthus-annuus-sunflower-seed-oil.body: Sunflower seed oil helps skin feel smoother and helps keep it moisturized. It supplies an oily, fatty-acid-rich component to creams, lotions and balms.
helianthus-annuus-sunflower-seed-oil.aliasNotes: Oil expressed from Helianthus annuus seeds.
helianthus-annuus-sunflower-seed-oil.distinctIngredients: Separate from sunflower seed wax, seed extract and isolated sunflower-oil derivatives.

helianthus-annuus-sunflower-seed-wax.name: Helianthus Annuus (Sunflower) Seed Wax
helianthus-annuus-sunflower-seed-wax.summary: Helps balms and sticks keep their shape.
helianthus-annuus-sunflower-seed-wax.body: Sunflower seed wax is a hard wax that gives products structure. It helps balms, sticks and other rich formulas stay firm rather than becoming too runny.
helianthus-annuus-sunflower-seed-wax.aliasNotes: Wax obtained from Helianthus annuus seeds.
helianthus-annuus-sunflower-seed-wax.distinctIngredients: Separate from liquid sunflower seed oil.

hydrogenated-polyisobutene.name: Hydrogenated Polyisobutene
hydrogenated-polyisobutene.summary: Softens skin and adjusts a product’s richness.
hydrogenated-polyisobutene.body: Hydrogenated polyisobutene is a synthetic oily ingredient that helps skin feel smooth. It can also change a product’s thickness and add shine, which is useful in lip products.
hydrogenated-polyisobutene.amountAndUse: Different grades have different weights and textures, from light liquids to more substantial oils.
hydrogenated-polyisobutene.aliasNotes: Hydrogenated polyisobutene, a synthetic hydrocarbon material.
hydrogenated-polyisobutene.distinctIngredients: Different from silicone oils and mineral oil, even when used for a similar texture.

hydrogenated-shea-butter.name: Hydrogenated Shea Butter
hydrogenated-shea-butter.summary: Conditions skin and adjusts a product’s thickness.
hydrogenated-shea-butter.body: Hydrogenated shea butter is shea butter that has been chemically treated with hydrogen. It helps condition skin and controls the consistency of a cream or balm.
hydrogenated-shea-butter.distinctIngredients: Separate from ordinary shea butter, shea oil and hydrogenated shea oil.

hydrogenated-vegetable-glycerides.name: Hydrogenated Vegetable Glycerides
hydrogenated-vegetable-glycerides.summary: Softens skin and builds a richer texture.
hydrogenated-vegetable-glycerides.body: Hydrogenated vegetable glycerides help skin feel smoother and give products body. Depending on the grade, they can contribute a waxy structure or a rich, jelly-like feel.
hydrogenated-vegetable-glycerides.amountAndUse: This name covers different mixtures and textures; the ingredient name alone does not specify one fixed consistency.
hydrogenated-vegetable-glycerides.aliasNotes: Hydrogenated glycerides derived from vegetable oils.
hydrogenated-vegetable-glycerides.distinctIngredients: Separate from unmodified vegetable oil and from hydrogenated vegetable oil.

isoamyl-cocoate.name: Isoamyl Cocoate
isoamyl-cocoate.summary: Softens skin with a light, less oily feel.
isoamyl-cocoate.body: Isoamyl cocoate is a liquid skin-softening ingredient that helps products spread smoothly. It is useful for giving creams and oils a lighter-feeling finish.
isoamyl-cocoate.aliasNotes: Ester made from isoamyl alcohol and coconut-oil fatty acids.
isoamyl-cocoate.distinctIngredients: Different from coconut oil and isoamyl laurate.

isoamyl-laurate.name: Isoamyl Laurate
isoamyl-laurate.summary: Adds a smooth feel and helps ingredients blend.
isoamyl-laurate.body: Isoamyl laurate softens skin and helps give products a light, silky texture. It can also help dissolve some sunscreen ingredients and spread pigments evenly through makeup.
isoamyl-laurate.distinctIngredients: Separate from isoamyl cocoate and from lauric acid.

isododecane.name: Isododecane
isododecane.summary: Helps products glide on, then evaporates.
isododecane.body: Isododecane helps products spread in a thin, light-feeling layer. It evaporates after application and can dissolve other ingredients, making it useful in makeup and makeup removers.
isododecane.aliasNotes: A branched hydrocarbon used as a volatile solvent.
isododecane.distinctIngredients: Separate from isohexadecane and from silicone ingredients.

isohexadecane.name: Isohexadecane
isohexadecane.summary: Adds glide and helps dissolve oily ingredients.
isohexadecane.body: Isohexadecane helps products spread smoothly and leaves skin with a light, velvety feel. As a solvent, it can also help dissolve oils and makeup in cleansing formulas.
isohexadecane.distinctIngredients: Different from isododecane and from silicones.

isononyl-isononanoate.name: Isononyl Isononanoate
isononyl-isononanoate.summary: Makes skin feel supple with a creamy finish.
isononyl-isononanoate.body: Isononyl isononanoate helps skin feel softer and more supple. It gives formulas a creamy feel without needing a heavy, waxy texture.
isononyl-isononanoate.aliasNotes: An ester of isononyl alcohol and isononanoic acid.

isostearyl-alcohol.name: Isostearyl Alcohol
isostearyl-alcohol.summary: Softens skin and helps control product texture.
isostearyl-alcohol.body: Isostearyl alcohol is a fatty alcohol used to make skin feel softer and smoother. It also helps adjust how thick or fluid a product feels.
isostearyl-alcohol.aliasNotes: Isooctadecan-1-ol, a branched long-chain fatty alcohol.
isostearyl-alcohol.distinctIngredients: Separate from stearyl alcohol and from ethanol.

jojoba-esters.name: Jojoba Esters
jojoba-esters.summary: Softens skin and adjusts a product’s texture.
jojoba-esters.body: Jojoba esters help skin feel smooth and soft. They are made by rearranging the wax components of jojoba oil, sometimes using hydrogenated jojoba oil too.
jojoba-esters.amountAndUse: Grades range from liquids to pastes and hard waxes, so the same ingredient name can contribute different textures.
jojoba-esters.aliasNotes: A mixture made by rearranging esters in jojoba oil and/or hydrogenated jojoba oil.
jojoba-esters.distinctIngredients: Different from unmodified jojoba seed oil.

jojoba-oil-macadamia-seed-oil-esters.name: Jojoba Oil/Macadamia Seed Oil Esters
jojoba-oil-macadamia-seed-oil-esters.summary: Helps skin feel smoother and more supple.
jojoba-oil-macadamia-seed-oil-esters.body: Jojoba oil/macadamia seed oil esters are modified fats made from the two named seed oils. They are used to condition skin and contribute a smooth, supple feel.
jojoba-oil-macadamia-seed-oil-esters.aliasNotes: Ester mixture formed by chemically rearranging jojoba and macadamia seed oils.
