rosmarinus-officinalis-rosemary-leaf-oil.aliasNotes: Essential oil from flowering tops and leaves of Rosmarinus officinalis.
rosmarinus-officinalis-rosemary-leaf-oil.distinctIngredients: Separate from Rosemary Leaf Extract and nonvolatile moisturizing plant oils.

sources.label: Allergic contact dermatitis to essential oils — DermNet

sphingomonas-ferment-extract.name: Sphingomonas Ferment Extract
sphingomonas-ferment-extract.summary: Fermentation extract that helps control texture and separation
sphingomonas-ferment-extract.body: Sphingomonas ferment extract helps control a formula’s thickness and keeps oil-and-water mixtures stable. It can also form a thin layer on skin, contributing to the product’s surface feel.
sphingomonas-ferment-extract.aliasNotes: Extract of a Sphingomonas fermentation product.
sphingomonas-ferment-extract.distinctIngredients: Keep separate from Sphingomonas Ferment Extract Filtrate; no live-probiotic identity is implied.

sources.label: SPHINGOMONAS FERMENT EXTRACT – Ingredient – COSMILE Europe

symphytum-officinale-callus-culture-extr.name: Symphytum Officinale Callus Culture Extract
symphytum-officinale-callus-culture-extr.summary: Cultured comfrey-cell extract used to condition skin
symphytum-officinale-callus-culture-extr.body: This ingredient is an extract of comfrey plant cells grown in culture. It is used to help keep skin in good condition; the phrase callus culture describes the plant tissue used to make it.
symphytum-officinale-callus-culture-extr.aliasNotes: Extract of cultured callus tissue from Symphytum officinale.
symphytum-officinale-callus-culture-extr.distinctIngredients: Separate from comfrey root or leaf extracts. A plant-cell extract is not a living human stem-cell ingredient.

sources.label: Symphytum Officinale Callus Culture Extract (with Product List)
SYMPHYTUM OFFICINALE CALLUS CULTURE EXTRACT – Ingredient – COSMILE Europe

tasmannia-lanceolata-fruit-leaf-extract.name: Tasmannia Lanceolata Fruit/Leaf Extract
tasmannia-lanceolata-fruit-leaf-extract.summary: Tasmanian pepper extract for antioxidants and skin comfort
tasmannia-lanceolata-fruit-leaf-extract.body: This extract from Tasmanian pepper fruit and leaves helps condition skin. It also contributes antioxidants, substances that help limit oxidation, a chemical process that changes molecules.
tasmannia-lanceolata-fruit-leaf-extract.aliasNotes: Combined fruit-and-leaf extract of Tasmannia lanceolata.
tasmannia-lanceolata-fruit-leaf-extract.distinctIngredients: Not culinary black pepper or a fruit-only Tasmanian pepper extract.

terminalia-ferdinandiana-fruit-extract.name: Terminalia Ferdinandiana Fruit Extract
terminalia-ferdinandiana-fruit-extract.summary: Kakadu-plum fruit extract that helps limit oxidation
terminalia-ferdinandiana-fruit-extract.body: This Kakadu-plum fruit extract is used for its antioxidant role, helping limit oxidation that can change ingredients. It is also listed for use in skin-brightening cosmetics.
terminalia-ferdinandiana-fruit-extract.aliasNotes: Extract of Terminalia ferdinandiana fruit pulp.
terminalia-ferdinandiana-fruit-extract.distinctIngredients: Separate from other plum species and from isolated vitamin C.

sources.label: Terminalia Ferdinandiana Fruit Extract (with Product List)
TERMINALIA FERDINANDIANA FRUIT EXTRACT – Ingredient – COSMILE Europe

tremella-fuciformis-sporocarp-extract.name: Tremella Fuciformis Sporocarp Extract
tremella-fuciformis-sporocarp-extract.summary: Mushroom extract that helps hold water near skin
tremella-fuciformis-sporocarp-extract.body: This mushroom extract helps retain water and leaves skin feeling moist and smooth. It contains polysaccharides, large sugar-based molecules that contribute to its water-holding properties.
tremella-fuciformis-sporocarp-extract.aliasNotes: Extract of the sporocarp, or fruiting body, of Tremella fuciformis.
tremella-fuciformis-sporocarp-extract.distinctIngredients: Not purified Tremella polysaccharide, mushroom powder or a ferment.

vitreoscilla-ferment.name: Vitreoscilla Ferment
vitreoscilla-ferment.summary: Fermentation-derived ingredient used to help condition skin
vitreoscilla-ferment.body: Vitreoscilla ferment is produced through fermentation using Vitreoscilla microorganisms. It is used in cosmetics to help keep skin in good condition, with the precise preparation depending on the raw material.
vitreoscilla-ferment.amountAndUse: The word ferment describes how the material is made; it does not establish that living bacteria remain in the product.
vitreoscilla-ferment.aliasNotes: Fermentation product of Vitreoscilla; no strain or live-cell count is specified.
vitreoscilla-ferment.distinctIngredients: Do not equate this generic INCI with a particular branded ferment or with live probiotics.

zingiber-officinale-ginger-root-extract.name: Zingiber Officinale (Ginger) Root Extract
zingiber-officinale-ginger-root-extract.summary: Ginger root extract with antioxidant and conditioning roles
zingiber-officinale-ginger-root-extract.body: Ginger root extract helps condition skin and supplies antioxidants, substances that help limit oxidation, a chemical process that changes molecules. Its aromatic components can also influence a formula’s scent.
zingiber-officinale-ginger-root-extract.aliasNotes: Root extract of Zingiber officinale as named on the page and roster.
zingiber-officinale-ginger-root-extract.distinctIngredients: Separate from ginger essential oil, ginger powder and isolated gingerol.

2-3-butanediol.name: 2,3-Butanediol
2-3-butanediol.summary: Helps hold water and dissolve other ingredients.
2-3-butanediol.body: 2,3-Butanediol helps a formula hold on to water and helps other ingredients dissolve. These supporting jobs make it useful in products built around a water-based mixture.
2-3-butanediol.detail: A humectant is an ingredient that attracts or retains water. Its solvent role means it also helps ingredients combine in the liquid part of a formula.
2-3-butanediol.aliasNotes: The numbered 2,3 form is preserved; it is not silently merged with other butanediol forms.
2-3-butanediol.distinctIngredients: Do not equate this record with the separate Butylene Glycol candidate.

acacia-senegal-gum.name: Acacia Senegal Gum
acacia-senegal-gum.summary: Thickens products and helps ingredients hold together.
acacia-senegal-gum.body: Acacia Senegal Gum gives a formula more body and helps its ingredients hold together. This tree-derived gum can also form a thin layer as a product dries.
acacia-senegal-gum.detail: In mixtures with xanthan gum, it can help adjust the sticky feel as well as the thickness. Its main role here is shaping the product’s texture.
acacia-senegal-gum.aliasNotes: Dried gum from Acacia senegal; this is not a broad acacia extract.

acetylated-glycol-stearate.name: Acetylated Glycol Stearate
acetylated-glycol-stearate.summary: Softens skin and helps keep lotions mixed.
acetylated-glycol-stearate.body: Acetylated Glycol Stearate helps skin feel softer and smoother. It also supports the mixture of oily and watery ingredients, helping a lotion or cream stay evenly blended.
acetylated-glycol-stearate.detail: An emulsion is a mixture of liquids that would normally separate, such as oil and water. This ingredient helps stabilize that mixture while contributing a soft skin feel.
acetylated-glycol-stearate.aliasNotes: Acetylated glycol stearate is retained as its own ingredient, distinct from glycol stearate.

acrylates-copolymer.name: Acrylates Copolymer
acrylates-copolymer.summary: Adjusts thickness or forms a thin layer.
acrylates-copolymer.body: Acrylates Copolymer helps control how a product feels and stays in place. Depending on the version used, it can thicken the formula or form a thin layer after application.
acrylates-copolymer.detail: The name covers polymers with different designs, so it does not identify one exact texture or level of hold. A polymer is a large molecule made from repeating smaller units.
acrylates-copolymer.amountAndUse: Its particular job depends on the polymer grade and the surrounding formula.

acrylates-crosspolymer.name: Acrylates/C10-30 Alkyl Acrylate Crosspolymer
acrylates-crosspolymer.summary: Thickens watery mixtures and helps keep oils dispersed.
acrylates-crosspolymer.body: Acrylates/C10-30 Alkyl Acrylate Crosspolymer gives watery formulas a thicker, gel-like texture. It also helps hold oil-containing mixtures together so they spread more consistently.
acrylates-crosspolymer.detail: Parts of this large molecule interact with water and other parts with oil. That combination makes it useful for both thickening and stabilizing a formula.
acrylates-crosspolymer.distinctIngredients: Not interchangeable with Acrylates Copolymer or Carbomer.

acrylates-dimethicone-copolymer.name: Acrylates/Dimethicone Copolymer
acrylates-dimethicone-copolymer.summary: Helps a product leave a flexible layer.
acrylates-dimethicone-copolymer.body: Acrylates/Dimethicone Copolymer helps a product form a flexible layer after it is applied. This can help a cosmetic finish hold together and stay in place.
acrylates-dimethicone-copolymer.detail: It is often supplied in a liquid carrier that evaporates, leaving the polymer behind. The result depends on the carrier and the rest of the formula.

alcohol.name: Alcohol
alcohol.summary: Dissolves ingredients and gives formulas a lighter feel.
alcohol.body: Alcohol helps dissolve ingredients that are difficult to mix into a formula. It can also make a product thinner and lighter-feeling when applied.
alcohol.detail: On a cosmetic ingredient list, Alcohol refers to ethanol. The amount used and the ingredients around it affect the character of the finished formula.
alcohol.caution: Alcohol-containing products can be drying, especially when skin is already dry. Consider how the finished product feels on your skin.
alcohol.aliasNotes: Alcohol here means ethanol; keep this record separate from denatured ethanol.
alcohol.distinctIngredients: Not the same ingredient identity as Alcohol Denat. or fatty alcohols such as cetyl alcohol.

sources.label: Your winter skin survival kit — American Academy of Dermatology

alcohol-denat.name: Alcohol Denat.
alcohol-denat.summary: Helps ingredients dissolve and formulas feel light.
alcohol-denat.body: Alcohol Denat. helps dissolve ingredients and creates a thinner, lighter-feeling formula. It is ethanol that has been denatured by adding substances that make it unsuitable to drink.
alcohol-denat.detail: Denatured identifies a particular form of alcohol, rather than a moisturizing fatty alcohol. The ingredient name alone does not specify which denaturing substances were used.
alcohol-denat.caution: Alcohol-containing products can be drying, especially when skin is already dry. Consider how the finished product feels on your skin.
alcohol-denat.aliasNotes: Denatured ethanol; retained separately from the Alcohol candidate.
alcohol-denat.distinctIngredients: Do not merge with Alcohol or with fatty alcohols.

sources.label: Your winter skin survival kit — American Academy of Dermatology

algin.name: Algin
algin.summary: Builds thickness and structure in watery products.
algin.body: Algin helps watery products thicken or set into a gel. Made from large sugar-based molecules obtained from brown seaweed, it gives a formula structure.
algin.detail: With calcium salts, it can form a firm gel, a useful property in setting masks. Different mixtures can therefore produce very different textures.
algin.aliasNotes: Algin candidate preserved as named; no broad algae-extract alias recorded.

alpha-isomethyl-ionone.name: Alpha-Isomethyl Ionone
alpha-isomethyl-ionone.body: Alpha-Isomethyl Ionone is used to give a cosmetic product part of its scent. It is one individual fragrance substance that may be combined with others to create the finished fragrance.
alpha-isomethyl-ionone.caution: Can cause an allergic skin reaction in some people. Avoid it if you know you are allergic to this ingredient.
alpha-isomethyl-ionone.aliasNotes: Specific fragrance chemical, not a collective name for all ionones.

alumina.name: Alumina
alumina.summary: Helps powders distribute evenly and adjusts texture.
alumina.body: Alumina can help pigments spread evenly through a formula and across skin. It can also absorb some oil or make a product less transparent, depending on how it is used.
alumina.detail: This is aluminum oxide, often used as part of a treated pigment system. Such systems help distribute pigments more evenly in the formula and during application.
alumina.distinctIngredients: Different from Aluminum Hydroxide and Aluminum Stearate.

aluminum-hydroxide.name: Aluminum Hydroxide
aluminum-hydroxide.summary: Helps shape pigment coverage and product appearance.
aluminum-hydroxide.body: Aluminum Hydroxide can be used to coat pigment particles or as part of a pigment base. It helps formulators control coverage and the appearance of a colored or opaque product.
aluminum-hydroxide.detail: Opaque means that you cannot see through the product. The ingredient can contribute to that effect, but its presence does not identify the complete pigment system.
aluminum-hydroxide.distinctIngredients: Not the same compound as Alumina.

aluminum-starch-octenylsuccinate.name: Aluminum Starch Octenylsuccinate
aluminum-starch-octenylsuccinate.summary: Absorbs oil and gives a smoother powdery feel.
aluminum-starch-octenylsuccinate.body: Aluminum Starch Octenylsuccinate is a modified starch powder that absorbs oil and helps powders resist clumping. It can make a cream or makeup product spread with a softer, less greasy feel.
aluminum-starch-octenylsuccinate.detail: Its texture depends on the amount used and the rest of the formula. The ingredient name describes a starch derivative, rather than ordinary unmodified starch.
aluminum-starch-octenylsuccinate.aliasNotes: Aluminum salt of modified starch; not interchangeable with plain starch.

aluminum-stearate.name: Aluminum Stearate
aluminum-stearate.summary: Thickens oily mixtures and helps prevent separation.
aluminum-stearate.body: Aluminum Stearate helps turn an oily liquid into a thicker, more structured mixture. It can also help keep emulsions stable and prevent powders from clumping together.
aluminum-stearate.detail: It is an aluminum salt of stearic acid. Its ability to form gels with oils makes it useful when a formula needs more body or needs to hold its shape.
aluminum-stearate.aliasNotes: Aluminum stearate salt; not stearic acid or another metal stearate.

behentrimonium-chloride.name: Behentrimonium Chloride
behentrimonium-chloride.summary: Helps condition hair or protect the formula.
behentrimonium-chloride.body: Behentrimonium Chloride helps hair feel softer and easier to comb, while reducing static. It also has a preservative role, helping protect a cosmetic formula from microbial spoilage.
behentrimonium-chloride.detail: Those are different possible uses of the same ingredient. A label listing alone cannot show whether conditioning, preservation or both motivated its use in a particular product.
behentrimonium-chloride.distinctIngredients: Do not merge with Behentrimonium Methosulfate or Cetrimonium Chloride.

benzoic-acid.name: Benzoic Acid
benzoic-acid.summary: Helps protect the formula during storage and use.
benzoic-acid.body: Benzoic Acid helps keep a cosmetic product from spoiling. It is commonly used alongside other preservatives so the formula’s preservation system can cover a broader range of microbes.
benzoic-acid.detail: A preservative blend combines ingredients with complementary roles to protect the contents of the container.

benzyl-alcohol.name: Benzyl Alcohol
benzyl-alcohol.summary: Helps preserve products and dissolve other ingredients.
benzyl-alcohol.body: Benzyl Alcohol helps protect a formula from spoilage and can help other ingredients dissolve. It may also contribute to scent, so its purpose can vary between products.
benzyl-alcohol.detail: It is a specific chemical with several formulation uses. Despite the shared word alcohol, it is not the same ingredient as ethanol or Alcohol Denat.
benzyl-alcohol.caution: Can cause an allergic skin reaction in some people. Avoid it if you know you are allergic to this ingredient.
benzyl-alcohol.distinctIngredients: Separate from Alcohol, Alcohol Denat. and Benzyl Benzoate.

benzyl-benzoate.name: Benzyl Benzoate
benzyl-benzoate.summary: Adds scent and helps fragrance ingredients dissolve.
benzyl-benzoate.body: Benzyl Benzoate can contribute a lightly sweet scent and help other ingredients dissolve. In a fragrance mixture, those roles help build the product’s overall smell and keep its ingredients combined.
benzyl-benzoate.caution: Can cause an allergic skin reaction in some people. Avoid it if you know you are allergic to this ingredient.
benzyl-benzoate.distinctIngredients: Not interchangeable with Benzoic Acid or Benzyl Alcohol.

butylene-glycol.name: Butylene Glycol
butylene-glycol.summary: Holds water and helps ingredients mix and spread.
butylene-glycol.body: Butylene Glycol helps dissolve other ingredients and attracts water, supporting a moisturized feel. It also helps a formula glide over skin instead of dragging during application.
butylene-glycol.detail: This ingredient is a small liquid molecule with several supporting jobs. How moisturizing or lightweight the finished product feels still depends on the complete formula.
butylene-glycol.aliasNotes: The read identifies the cosmetic Butylene Glycol record as 1,3-butanediol forms.
butylene-glycol.distinctIngredients: Do not merge with the separately named 2,3-Butanediol candidate.

capryloyl-glycine.name: Capryloyl Glycine
capryloyl-glycine.summary: Helps oily material mix with water during cleansing.
capryloyl-glycine.body: Capryloyl Glycine can help a cleansing formula lift oily material so it can mix with water. It is made from a fatty-acid component joined to glycine, an amino acid.
capryloyl-glycine.detail: Its surface-active properties help it work where water meets oily material, supporting the cleansing mixture.
capryloyl-glycine.distinctIngredients: Not the same as unmodified Glycine.

caprylyl-methicone.name: Caprylyl Methicone
caprylyl-methicone.summary: Helps a product glide without a heavy feel.
caprylyl-methicone.body: Caprylyl Methicone is a lightweight silicone liquid that helps products spread smoothly. It can give a formula a silky feel and then evaporate from the surface.
caprylyl-methicone.detail: It works with both silicone ingredients and plant oils, making it useful in mixed oil formulas. The final finish depends on the other ingredients left behind.
caprylyl-methicone.aliasNotes: Specific caprylyl-modified silicone; not a synonym for all silicones.

carrageenan.name: Carrageenan
carrageenan.summary: Thickens watery products and helps them hold together.
carrageenan.body: Carrageenan is a seaweed-derived ingredient that helps thicken a formula or turn it into a gel. It also helps a mixture hold its texture instead of becoming uneven.
carrageenan.detail: It is made of large sugar-based molecules obtained from red seaweeds. These molecules help give the product its structure.
carrageenan.aliasNotes: Carrageenan retained as named; not broadly equated with seaweed extracts.

cellulose-gum.name: Cellulose Gum
cellulose-gum.summary: Adds thickness and helps keep lotions evenly mixed.
cellulose-gum.body: Cellulose Gum helps a product become thicker and more stable. In a lotion, it supports the mixture of oil and water so the texture stays more even.
cellulose-gum.detail: It is a modified form of cellulose, the structural material in plant cell walls. Changing cellulose gives it useful properties for controlling the thickness of a cosmetic formula.
cellulose-gum.aliasNotes: This record is the sodium salt of carboxymethylated cellulose.
cellulose-gum.distinctIngredients: Keep separate from Hydroxyethylcellulose and Ethylcellulose.

ceteareth-12.name: Ceteareth-12
ceteareth-12.summary: Helps water and oil combine in one formula.
ceteareth-12.body: Ceteareth-12 helps oily and watery ingredients mix into a cream or lotion. This makes it easier to combine ingredients that would otherwise tend to separate.
ceteareth-12.detail: It is an emulsifier, meaning a mixing helper for oil and water. The number is part of its chemical identity and distinguishes it from other ceteareth ingredients.
ceteareth-12.distinctIngredients: Ceteareth-12 is distinct from Ceteareth-25 and Cetearyl Alcohol.

ceteareth-25.name: Ceteareth-25
ceteareth-25.summary: Helps combine oil and water in a product.
ceteareth-25.body: Ceteareth-25 helps oily ingredients mix with water and can contribute to cleansing. It is useful when a formula needs to keep a smooth mixture rather than separate into layers.
ceteareth-25.detail: The number identifies a particular member of the ceteareth family. It is part of the ingredient’s name, not a percentage or a measure of product strength.
ceteareth-25.distinctIngredients: Not interchangeable with Ceteareth-12 or Cetearyl Alcohol.

cetearyl-olivate.name: Cetearyl Olivate
cetearyl-olivate.summary: Helps oily and watery ingredients blend together.
cetearyl-olivate.body: Cetearyl Olivate helps oil and water combine in a cream or lotion. It is made by joining cetearyl alcohol with fatty acids obtained from olive oil.
cetearyl-olivate.detail: It is often paired with Sorbitan Olivate as an emulsifying blend. Evidence about that whole blend should not automatically be treated as evidence for Cetearyl Olivate alone.
cetearyl-olivate.aliasNotes: Ester of cetearyl alcohol and olive-oil fatty acids; not olive oil itself.
cetearyl-olivate.distinctIngredients: Olivem 1000 is a blend containing this ingredient, not an exact ingredient alias.

cetrimonium-bromide.name: Cetrimonium Bromide
cetrimonium-bromide.summary: Helps preserve a formula and keep ingredients mixed.
cetrimonium-bromide.body: Cetrimonium Bromide can help protect a cosmetic product from microbial spoilage. It also helps oily and watery ingredients combine and can reduce static in hair products.
cetrimonium-bromide.detail: These are formulation and conditioning roles. Which one matters most depends on the particular product and how the ingredient is combined with other materials.
cetrimonium-bromide.distinctIngredients: Keep the bromide separate from Cetrimonium Chloride.

cetyl-peg-ppg-10-1-dimethicone.name: Cetyl PEG/PPG-10/1 Dimethicone
cetyl-peg-ppg-10-1-dimethicone.summary: Helps water and silicone oils stay blended.
cetyl-peg-ppg-10-1-dimethicone.body: Cetyl PEG/PPG-10/1 Dimethicone helps water combine with silicone oils in a formula. It supports an even cream or lotion instead of leaving those ingredients in separate layers.
cetyl-peg-ppg-10-1-dimethicone.detail: This is a silicone-based emulsifier: an ingredient designed to bridge ingredients that do not naturally mix. The full name identifies a particular modified silicone.
cetyl-peg-ppg-10-1-dimethicone.aliasNotes: Specific cetyl PEG/PPG-10/1 dimethicone; numerical identity preserved.
cetyl-peg-ppg-10-1-dimethicone.distinctIngredients: Not equivalent to plain Dimethicone or other numbered PEG/PPG dimethicones.

chlorphenesin.name: Chlorphenesin
chlorphenesin.summary: Helps keep microbes from spoiling the product.
chlorphenesin.body: Chlorphenesin helps protect a cosmetic formula from microbial spoilage during storage and use. It is often paired with another preservative to build the product’s preservation system.
chlorphenesin.detail: Its role is protecting the contents of the container, and it is often combined with phenoxyethanol in a preservation system.

citric-acid.name: Citric Acid
citric-acid.summary: Adjusts acidity so the formula works as intended.
citric-acid.body: Citric Acid is often added in small amounts to adjust a product’s acidity, or pH. Getting that balance right helps the other ingredients work together in the intended formula.
citric-acid.detail: Its presence does not automatically make a product an exfoliating acid treatment. The amount and the finished pH matter when deciding what job an acid is doing.

cocamidopropyl-betaine.name: Cocamidopropyl Betaine
cocamidopropyl-betaine.summary: Helps wash away oily dirt and support lather.
cocamidopropyl-betaine.body: Cocamidopropyl Betaine is a cleansing ingredient that helps a wash lift oily dirt. It also helps bubbles stay stable, shaping the lather when it is blended with other cleansers.
cocamidopropyl-betaine.detail: Formulators combine cleansing ingredients to balance cleaning, foam and feel. That means this ingredient’s presence alone does not tell you how strong or how foamy the finished wash will be.
cocamidopropyl-betaine.caution: Some people develop contact allergy to products containing this ingredient. Avoid it if you have a confirmed allergy.
cocamidopropyl-betaine.distinctIngredients: Not interchangeable with Coco-Betaine, Cocamidopropyl Dimethylamine or plain Betaine.

sources.label: Contact allergy to cocamidopropyl betaine — DermNet

cocamidopropyl-dimethylamine.name: Cocamidopropyl Dimethylamine
cocamidopropyl-dimethylamine.summary: Helps ingredients mix and can support foaming.
cocamidopropyl-dimethylamine.body: Cocamidopropyl Dimethylamine helps a formula mix and can contribute to cleansing and foam. It can also be used in specific blends to help an ingredient such as salicylic acid dissolve.
cocamidopropyl-dimethylamine.detail: Its job can therefore differ between a cleanser and a leave-on formula. Seeing it on a label does not prove that a particular branded blend has been used.
cocamidopropyl-dimethylamine.aliasNotes: Coco-derived amidopropyl dimethylamine, distinct from its betaine derivative.
cocamidopropyl-dimethylamine.distinctIngredients: Not Cocamidopropyl Betaine; Curcylic 40 is a blend rather than an exact alias.

coco-betaine.name: Coco-Betaine
coco-betaine.summary: Helps wash away oily dirt and build lather.
coco-betaine.body: Coco-Betaine helps a cleanser mix oily dirt with water so it can be washed away. It can also improve the volume or staying power of the foam and help control thickness.
coco-betaine.detail: It is one of several ingredients a formulator may combine to shape a wash’s cleansing and lather. It should not be confused with similarly named betaine ingredients.
coco-betaine.distinctIngredients: Coco-Betaine is distinct from Cocamidopropyl Betaine and plain Betaine.

coco-glucoside.name: Coco-Glucoside
coco-glucoside.summary: Helps wash away oily dirt and create lather.
coco-glucoside.body: Coco-Glucoside is a cleansing ingredient that helps a wash remove oily dirt. It also helps make a stable lather, contributing to how the product feels as it is used.
coco-glucoside.detail: It is made from glucose and coconut-derived fatty alcohol components. This describes the ingredient’s chemistry, rather than making the finished cleanser equivalent to coconut oil or sugar.
coco-glucoside.caution: People with contact allergy to decyl glucoside may also react to coco-glucoside. A dermatologist can advise which ingredients to avoid.
coco-glucoside.distinctIngredients: Not the same ingredient as Decyl Glucoside or Coco-Betaine.

sources.label: Patient information leaflet: decyl glucoside — European Society of Contact Dermatitis

decyl-glucoside.name: Decyl Glucoside
decyl-glucoside.summary: Helps oily dirt rinse away and supports foam.
decyl-glucoside.body: Decyl Glucoside helps a cleanser lift oily dirt and rinse it away with water. It also contributes foam, making it useful in face, body and hair washes.
decyl-glucoside.detail: It is made by joining glucose with decyl alcohol. The full formula determines the feel of the wash, including how much it lathers and how it rinses.
decyl-glucoside.caution: Avoid it if you have a confirmed contact allergy to decyl glucoside. A dermatologist can help identify which related glucosides you also need to avoid.
decyl-glucoside.distinctIngredients: Retained separately from Coco-Glucoside and other glucosides.

sources.label: Patient information leaflet: decyl glucoside — European Society of Contact Dermatitis

dehydroacetic-acid.name: Dehydroacetic Acid
dehydroacetic-acid.summary: Helps keep fungi from spoiling the product.
dehydroacetic-acid.body: Dehydroacetic Acid helps preserve a cosmetic formula, particularly against fungi. It supports the preservation system that keeps the contents from spoiling during storage and ordinary use.
dehydroacetic-acid.detail: Its activity is not identical against every type of microbe. Formulators can combine preservatives to meet the needs of a specific formula.
dehydroacetic-acid.aliasNotes: Dehydroacetic Acid is retained as the acid, not its sodium salt or a preservative blend.

diethylhexyl-syringylidenemalonate.name: Diethylhexyl Syringylidenemalonate
diethylhexyl-syringylidenemalonate.summary: Helps ingredients resist changes caused by light.
diethylhexyl-syringylidenemalonate.body: Diethylhexyl Syringylidenemalonate helps protect a formula from light-related changes. It can help keep color more consistent and support the stability of certain light-sensitive ingredients.
diethylhexyl-syringylidenemalonate.detail: This type of helper is called a photostabilizer. Supporting the stability of a sunscreen ingredient is different from establishing the protection level of a finished sunscreen.

dilinoleic-acid-propanediol-copolymer.name: Dilinoleic Acid/Propanediol Copolymer
dilinoleic-acid-propanediol-copolymer.summary: Adds a rich feel and a glossy finish.
dilinoleic-acid-propanediol-copolymer.body: Dilinoleic Acid/Propanediol Copolymer adds softness and a slightly clingy, glossy feel. It helps a product stay on the surface, which is useful when a formula is designed for a rich finish.
dilinoleic-acid-propanediol-copolymer.detail: It may be blended with other fats and plant-derived ingredients to build a richer texture. Properties of a complete commercial blend should not be assigned to this ingredient alone.
dilinoleic-acid-propanediol-copolymer.aliasNotes: Copolymer of dilinoleic acid and propanediol, not either starting material alone.

dimethicone-crosspolymer.name: Dimethicone Crosspolymer
dimethicone-crosspolymer.summary: Thickens formulas and gives them a smooth glide.
dimethicone-crosspolymer.body: Dimethicone Crosspolymer helps thicken a formula while giving it a silky, smooth feel. Its springy silicone structure can add body without relying only on heavier oils or waxes.
dimethicone-crosspolymer.detail: It is commonly blended with a liquid silicone carrier. The carrier and the polymer work together to determine how the finished product spreads and feels.
dimethicone-crosspolymer.aliasNotes: Crosslinked silicone polymer, retained separately from unmodified Dimethicone.
dimethicone-crosspolymer.distinctIngredients: Not interchangeable with the other specifically named dimethicone crosspolymers in this corpus.

dimethicone-bis-isobutyl-ppg-20-crosspol.name: Dimethicone/Bis-Isobutyl PPG-20 Crosspolymer
dimethicone-bis-isobutyl-ppg-20-crosspol.summary: Softens skin feel and adjusts formula thickness.
dimethicone-bis-isobutyl-ppg-20-crosspol.body: Dimethicone/Bis-Isobutyl PPG-20 Crosspolymer helps a product feel soft and smooth on skin. It also lets formulators adjust thickness, shaping how easily a cream or serum spreads.
dimethicone-bis-isobutyl-ppg-20-crosspol.detail: This is a specifically modified, crosslinked silicone polymer. Crosslinked means its long molecules are connected into a larger network, rather than being separate liquid silicone chains.
dimethicone-bis-isobutyl-ppg-20-crosspol.distinctIngredients: Full Bis-Isobutyl PPG-20 identity retained; not a generic Dimethicone Crosspolymer alias.

dimethicone-vinyl-dimethicone-crosspolym.name: Dimethicone/Vinyl Dimethicone Crosspolymer
dimethicone-vinyl-dimethicone-crosspolym.summary: Adds a silky finish and absorbs some oil.
dimethicone-vinyl-dimethicone-crosspolym.body: Dimethicone/Vinyl Dimethicone Crosspolymer is a silicone powder that gives products a silky, powdery feel. It can also absorb some oil, helping shape the finish on skin.
dimethicone-vinyl-dimethicone-crosspolym.detail: It is an elastic, crosslinked silicone material. Its texture contribution depends on how it is dispersed and what liquid ingredients are around it.
dimethicone-vinyl-dimethicone-crosspolym.distinctIngredients: Keep separate from Dimethicone Crosspolymer and Dimethicone/Bis-Isobutyl PPG-20 Crosspolymer.

dimethiconol.name: Dimethiconol
dimethiconol.summary: Leaves a smooth, silky layer on the surface.
dimethiconol.body: Dimethiconol helps a product leave a silky, smooth film on skin. It is a thick silicone commonly mixed with a lighter liquid silicone to make it easier to spread.
dimethiconol.detail: The film contributes softness and a less greasy feel in suitable blends. The ingredient is usually experienced as part of that mixture, rather than as a thick silicone on its own.
dimethiconol.distinctIngredients: Dimethiconol is distinct from Dimethicone and from crosslinked dimethicone polymers.

dimethyl-isosorbide.name: Dimethyl Isosorbide
dimethyl-isosorbide.summary: Helps ingredients dissolve into a workable formula.
dimethyl-isosorbide.body: Dimethyl Isosorbide helps dissolve ingredients so they can be incorporated into a formula. It can also help adjust the liquid’s thickness and the way ingredients are carried within it.
dimethyl-isosorbide.detail: A solvent is a liquid used to dissolve other materials. Its presence does not establish that every active ingredient in a product reaches a particular depth in skin.

disodium-phosphate.name: Disodium Phosphate
disodium-phosphate.summary: Keeps the formula’s acidity within its intended range.
disodium-phosphate.body: Disodium Phosphate helps control a product’s acidity, also called pH. It works as a buffer, helping keep that balance suitable for the other ingredients in the formula.
disodium-phosphate.aliasNotes: Disodium phosphate identity retained, not a blanket record for all phosphates.

disodium-stearoyl-glutamate.name: Disodium Stearoyl Glutamate
disodium-stearoyl-glutamate.summary: Helps oily material mix with water.
disodium-stearoyl-glutamate.body: Disodium Stearoyl Glutamate is a cleansing helper that helps oily material mix with water. Its structure joins a fatty-acid component to a glutamic-acid-derived part, giving it useful surface-active properties.
disodium-stearoyl-glutamate.detail: Surface-active means working at the boundary between liquids such as oil and water. This ingredient has its own identity and should not be merged with similarly named glutamate salts.
disodium-stearoyl-glutamate.distinctIngredients: Not Sodium Stearoyl Glutamate or unmodified Glutamic Acid.

disteardimonium-hectorite.name: Disteardimonium Hectorite
disteardimonium-hectorite.summary: Thickens products and helps keep powders evenly dispersed.
disteardimonium-hectorite.body: Disteardimonium Hectorite is a modified clay that makes formulas less runny. It can help keep pigments suspended instead of settling to the bottom during storage.
disteardimonium-hectorite.detail: Keeping powders evenly dispersed helps maintain a consistent texture as the product is used.
disteardimonium-hectorite.aliasNotes: Organically modified hectorite clay; not plain Hectorite.

ethoxydiglycol.name: Ethoxydiglycol
ethoxydiglycol.summary: Helps hard-to-dissolve ingredients mix into the formula.
ethoxydiglycol.body: Ethoxydiglycol helps dissolve ingredients that would otherwise be difficult to incorporate. That makes it useful for creating an even mixture in products containing certain active ingredients.
ethoxydiglycol.detail: A solvent is a liquid that dissolves other materials. The choice of solvent depends on which ingredients need to be incorporated.

ethylcellulose.name: Ethylcellulose
ethylcellulose.summary: Thickens products and helps form a surface layer.
ethylcellulose.body: Ethylcellulose helps give a formula body and can form a thin layer as it dries. It is a modified plant-cellulose material used when a product needs more structure or film formation.
ethylcellulose.detail: Different grades are available for different textures. A supplier’s film-forming cosmetic grade supports this basic role, without identifying the grade used in every finished product.
ethylcellulose.distinctIngredients: Ethylcellulose is distinct from Cellulose Gum and Hydroxyethylcellulose.

ethylene-acrylic-acid-copolymer.name: Ethylene/Acrylic Acid Copolymer
ethylene-acrylic-acid-copolymer.summary: Helps products hold together and form a film.
ethylene-acrylic-acid-copolymer.body: Ethylene/Acrylic Acid Copolymer helps keep a formula stable and can form a thin layer after application. It can also bind powder ingredients together or make a mixture look less transparent.
ethylene-acrylic-acid-copolymer.detail: A copolymer is a large molecule built from more than one kind of repeating unit. Its role here is controlling a product’s structure and finish.
ethylene-acrylic-acid-copolymer.distinctIngredients: Not interchangeable with Acrylates Copolymer or free Acrylic Acid.

ethylhexyl-polyhydroxystearate.name: Ethylhexyl Polyhydroxystearate
ethylhexyl-polyhydroxystearate.summary: Helps skin feel smoother and more supple.
ethylhexyl-polyhydroxystearate.body: Ethylhexyl Polyhydroxystearate helps a product leave skin feeling soft and smooth. It is an emollient, a fatty-textured ingredient used to improve the feel of a formula on skin.
ethylhexyl-polyhydroxystearate.detail: It is an ester made from 2-ethylhexanol and polyhydroxystearic acid. That full identity distinguishes it from related ingredients with similar-looking names.
ethylhexyl-polyhydroxystearate.distinctIngredients: Not Polyhydroxystearic Acid or Acetyl Ethylhexyl Polyhydroxystearate.

fragrance.name: Fragrance
fragrance.summary: Gives the product its intended scent.
fragrance.body: Fragrance is a collective label for ingredients used to scent a product. The mixture can be simple or complex, and the word alone does not identify every fragrance substance inside.
fragrance.detail: Different products can list Fragrance while using very different scent mixtures. Contacting the manufacturer may help when you need to check for a particular fragrance ingredient.
fragrance.caution: Fragrance mixtures can cause allergic reactions in some people. Avoid a mixture if it contains a fragrance ingredient you know you are allergic to.
fragrance.aliasNotes: Collective fragrance declaration, not one chemically defined ingredient.

glyceryl-acrylate-acrylic-acid-copolymer.name: Glyceryl Acrylate/Acrylic Acid Copolymer
glyceryl-acrylate-acrylic-acid-copolymer.summary: Holds water and gives products a gel texture.
glyceryl-acrylate-acrylic-acid-copolymer.body: Glyceryl Acrylate/Acrylic Acid Copolymer helps a product hold water while adding a smooth, gel-like texture. It can leave a water-rich layer that contributes to a moisturized feel.
glyceryl-acrylate-acrylic-acid-copolymer.detail: The ingredient is a large polymer with glycerin-related groups attached to it. Those groups help it interact with water, while the polymer provides structure.
glyceryl-acrylate-acrylic-acid-copolymer.distinctIngredients: Not an exact synonym for Carbomer, Acrylic Acid or Glycerin.

glyceryl-caprylate.name: Glyceryl Caprylate
glyceryl-caprylate.summary: Softens skin feel and helps oil mix with water.
glyceryl-caprylate.body: Glyceryl Caprylate helps skin feel softer and supports the mixing of oil and water. It often works beside other emulsifiers, the ingredients that hold a cream or lotion together.
glyceryl-caprylate.detail: It is an ester of glycerin and caprylic acid. This gives it a different set of formulation properties from either glycerin or the fatty acid on its own.
glyceryl-caprylate.distinctIngredients: Not Glyceryl Caprate, Caprylic Acid or Glycerin.

glyceryl-stearate-citrate.name: Glyceryl Stearate Citrate
glyceryl-stearate-citrate.summary: Softens skin and helps keep oil and water mixed.
glyceryl-stearate-citrate.body: Glyceryl Stearate Citrate helps oily and watery ingredients combine in a cream or lotion. It also gives the product a softening feel on skin.
glyceryl-stearate-citrate.detail: It is related to glyceryl stearate but has an additional citric-acid-derived part in its structure. That difference is why the complete ingredient name is worth keeping separate.
glyceryl-stearate-citrate.distinctIngredients: Distinct from Glyceryl Stearate, Glyceryl Stearate SE and Citric Acid.

glyceryl-stearate-se.name: Glyceryl Stearate SE
glyceryl-stearate-se.summary: Helps oil and water form a smooth cream.
glyceryl-stearate-se.body: Glyceryl Stearate SE helps oily and watery ingredients blend into a cream or lotion. It can also leave skin feeling smoother and softer.
glyceryl-stearate-se.detail: SE means self-emulsifying. This grade contains a small amount of water-friendly soap components that help glyceryl stearate mix with water more readily.
glyceryl-stearate-se.aliasNotes: Self-emulsifying glyceryl stearate grade, with soap components; SE is part of the identity.
glyceryl-stearate-se.distinctIngredients: Not interchangeable with plain Glyceryl Stearate or Glyceryl Stearate Citrate.

glycol-distearate.name: Glycol Distearate
glycol-distearate.summary: Makes washes look pearly and adds body.
glycol-distearate.body: Glycol Distearate gives some cleansers their milky, pearly appearance. It can also add body to a cream or lotion, helping shape how thick the product feels.
glycol-distearate.detail: A pearling agent changes how the product looks rather than supplying the cleanser’s main cleaning action. It is made from stearic acid and ethylene glycol joined into an ester.
glycol-distearate.distinctIngredients: Not Glycol Stearate or Acetylated Glycol Stearate.

gold.name: Gold
gold.summary: Adds metallic color or visual detail to products.
gold.body: Gold can be included to change a cosmetic product’s appearance, such as its color or visible metallic detail.
gold.caution: Gold can cause an allergic skin reaction in some people. Avoid it if you have a known gold allergy.
gold.aliasNotes: Metallic Gold record; does not specify particle size or a particular dispersion.
gold.distinctIngredients: Do not automatically merge with Colloidal Gold, gold salts or named gold complexes.

hexylene-glycol.name: Hexylene Glycol
hexylene-glycol.summary: Helps ingredients dissolve and thick mixtures spread.
hexylene-glycol.body: Hexylene Glycol helps dissolve other ingredients and can thin a formula that would otherwise feel too thick. This supports easier spreading and a more workable liquid texture.
hexylene-glycol.detail: It can also be used within particular preservative blends. A product listing Hexylene Glycol does not identify the whole blend or show what each ingredient contributes to preservation.
hexylene-glycol.aliasNotes: Specific 2-methylpentane-2,4-diol identity; not a generic glycol record.

hydroxyacetophenone.name: Hydroxyacetophenone
hydroxyacetophenone.summary: Helps limit oxidation and supports product preservation.
hydroxyacetophenone.body: Hydroxyacetophenone helps protect a formula against oxidation, the changes that occur when ingredients react with oxygen. It can also support the work of the formula’s preservatives.
hydroxyacetophenone.detail: An antioxidant and a preservative booster do different jobs. One limits oxygen-related changes; the other helps the system used to control microbial spoilage.
hydroxyacetophenone.aliasNotes: The read identifies p-hydroxyacetophenone; not all hydroxyacetophenone isomers.

hydroxyethyl-acrylate-sodium-acryloyldim.name: Hydroxyethyl Acrylate/Sodium Acryloyldimethyl Taurate Copolymer
hydroxyethyl-acrylate-sodium-acryloyldim.summary: Builds a gel texture and keeps oils dispersed.
hydroxyethyl-acrylate-sodium-acryloyldim.body: Hydroxyethyl Acrylate/Sodium Acryloyldimethyl Taurate Copolymer thickens water-based products and helps keep oil droplets mixed in. It is useful for making a smooth gel or lotion with a flexible texture.
hydroxyethyl-acrylate-sodium-acryloyldim.detail: The long name identifies a large polymer that gives the formula structure. Its thickening and stabilizing roles can work together when a product contains both watery and oily ingredients.
hydroxyethyl-acrylate-sodium-acryloyldim.aliasNotes: Exact sodium acryloyldimethyl taurate copolymer retained.

sources.label: Hydroxyethyl Acrylate/Sodium Acryloyldimethyl Taurate Copolymer — INKEEDecoder

hydroxyethylcellulose.name: Hydroxyethylcellulose
hydroxyethylcellulose.summary: Thickens watery products and helps them spread smoothly.
hydroxyethylcellulose.body: Hydroxyethylcellulose adds thickness and a smooth glide to cosmetic products. It is particularly useful for turning a runny water-based mixture into a more manageable gel.
hydroxyethylcellulose.detail: It is a modified form of cellulose, the material that gives plant cell walls structure. The modification helps it work as a thickener in a formula.
hydroxyethylcellulose.distinctIngredients: Keep separate from Cellulose Gum, Ethylcellulose and Hydroxyethyl Ethylcellulose.

hydroxypropyl-cyclodextrin.name: Hydroxypropyl Cyclodextrin
hydroxypropyl-cyclodextrin.summary: Helps hold other ingredients within the formula.
hydroxypropyl-cyclodextrin.body: Hydroxypropyl Cyclodextrin can hold other ingredients inside its ring-shaped structure. This makes it useful as a carrier when a formulator wants to package an ingredient within another material.
hydroxypropyl-cyclodextrin.detail: Its outside interacts readily with water, while its inner pocket can accommodate more oil-loving molecules.
hydroxypropyl-cyclodextrin.aliasNotes: Hydroxypropyl-modified cyclodextrin record; not plain Cyclodextrin.

inulin-lauryl-carbamate.name: Inulin Lauryl Carbamate
inulin-lauryl-carbamate.summary: Keeps oil droplets and particles from clumping.
inulin-lauryl-carbamate.body: Inulin Lauryl Carbamate helps oil droplets stay mixed into water-based formulas. It can also help particles that do not dissolve in water remain evenly dispersed instead of gathering into clumps.
inulin-lauryl-carbamate.detail: It is made by adding oil-friendly parts to inulin, a large sugar-based molecule. The resulting ingredient works as an emulsifier and stabilizer.
inulin-lauryl-carbamate.aliasNotes: Chemically modified inulin, not unmodified Inulin.

iron-oxides.name: Iron Oxides
iron-oxides.summary: Adds red, yellow or black tones to products.
iron-oxides.body: Iron Oxides are pigments used to color makeup and other cosmetics. Combining red, yellow and black iron oxides lets formulators create a wide range of skin-tone shades.
iron-oxides.detail: The plural name covers a pigment group rather than one single oxide. The exact colors and proportions determine the visible shade of the finished product.
iron-oxides.aliasNotes: Collective pigment group comprising red, yellow and black iron oxide records; no single member substituted for the group.
iron-oxides.distinctIngredients: CI 77491, CI 77492 and CI 77499 identify different members, not individually interchangeable aliases.

isoceteth-20.name: Isoceteth-20
isoceteth-20.summary: Helps oily ingredients mix into watery products.
isoceteth-20.body: Isoceteth-20 helps incorporate oil-loving ingredients, including fragrance, into water-based products. It supports an even mixture where the ingredients would otherwise be difficult to combine.
isoceteth-20.detail: This is a solubilizer or emulsifier, meaning a mixing helper. The full name identifies a particular ingredient rather than all isoceteths or fatty alcohols.
isoceteth-20.distinctIngredients: Retain Isoceteth-20 separately from other numbered isoceteth ingredients.

isopentyldiol.name: Isopentyldiol
isopentyldiol.summary: Helps hold water and leaves a smooth feel.
isopentyldiol.body: Isopentyldiol helps a formula hold moisture and dissolve other ingredients. It can also contribute a smooth skin feel with less stickiness.
isopentyldiol.detail: It is a water-soluble liquid with both solvent and moisture-holding roles. Its contribution depends on how much is used and the ingredients it is combined with.
isopentyldiol.aliasNotes: Isopentyldiol as named; do not equate all five-carbon diols.

lactic-acid-glycolic-acid-copolymer.name: Lactic Acid/Glycolic Acid Copolymer
lactic-acid-glycolic-acid-copolymer.summary: Can form part of a system carrying other ingredients.
lactic-acid-glycolic-acid-copolymer.body: Lactic Acid/Glycolic Acid Copolymer is a large molecule made by linking lactic-acid and glycolic-acid units. It can be used within carrier systems that package other cosmetic ingredients.
lactic-acid-glycolic-acid-copolymer.detail: A supplier documents it in multicomponent peptide-delivery blends. That supports a carrier-system use, but does not show that every product containing it uses the same delivery system.
lactic-acid-glycolic-acid-copolymer.evidence: Carrier use is illustrated by supplier blend documentation, not a test of this ingredient alone.
lactic-acid-glycolic-acid-copolymer.aliasNotes: Linked copolymer form, not a simple mixture of free lactic acid and free glycolic acid.
lactic-acid-glycolic-acid-copolymer.distinctIngredients: Do not treat as the exfoliating Lactic Acid or Glycolic Acid ingredient.

sources.label: LACTIC ACID/GLYCOLIC ACID COPOLYMER — COSMILE Europe
Anti-Aging: Go Beyond Beauty — Coast Southwest / Infinitec

lauroyl-lysine.name: Lauroyl Lysine
lauroyl-lysine.summary: Helps products glide and powders spread evenly.
lauroyl-lysine.body: Lauroyl Lysine gives products a smoother, silkier feel and helps powder ingredients distribute evenly. It is useful when a cream or makeup formula needs less drag during application.
lauroyl-lysine.detail: This ingredient combines a fatty-acid part with lysine, an amino acid. In a supplier’s pure Lauroyl Lysine powder, its crystal shape supports the texture and pigment-dispersing roles.
lauroyl-lysine.aliasNotes: Lauroyl derivative of lysine; not free Lysine.

linalool.name: Linalool
linalool.summary: Contributes scent to the finished product.
linalool.body: Linalool is a fragrance ingredient that helps create a product’s scent. It can be present in botanical fragrant oils as well as in fragrance mixtures assembled from individual ingredients.
linalool.caution: Can cause an allergic skin reaction in some people. Avoid it if you know you are allergic to linalool.
linalool.aliasNotes: Specific fragrance molecule, not a collective term for lavender or other essential oils.

magnesium-sulfate.name: Magnesium Sulfate
magnesium-sulfate.summary: Adjusts thickness and helps certain creams stay mixed.
magnesium-sulfate.body: Magnesium Sulfate helps control a formula’s thickness and can stabilize some creams. It is particularly useful in mixtures where tiny water droplets are held within a continuous oily phase.
magnesium-sulfate.detail: This type of mixture is called a water-in-oil emulsion. Magnesium sulfate helps adjust the structure of such formulations.
magnesium-sulfate.aliasNotes: Magnesium sulfate identity retained; the name alone does not specify hydration state.

manganese-gluconate.name: Manganese Gluconate
manganese-gluconate.body: Manganese Gluconate is a manganese salt used as a skin-conditioning ingredient. It is included to help maintain the condition of skin, within the broader moisturizing or care formula.
manganese-gluconate.aliasNotes: Manganese salt of gluconic acid; not free manganese or other gluconate salts.

methylparaben.name: Methylparaben
methylparaben.summary: Helps keep microbes from spoiling a formula.
methylparaben.body: Methylparaben is a preservative that helps keep cosmetic products from spoiling. It is used to protect the formula during storage and use, often as one part of a preservation system.
methylparaben.detail: Methylparaben is one particular member of the paraben family. Its name should be kept separate from other parabens when checking an ingredient list.
methylparaben.aliasNotes: Methyl ester of 4-hydroxybenzoic acid; specific paraben retained.
methylparaben.distinctIngredients: Not a collective record for all parabens.

methylpropanediol.name: Methylpropanediol
methylpropanediol.summary: Helps ingredients dissolve and improves the product’s feel.
methylpropanediol.body: Methylpropanediol helps other ingredients dissolve into a formula. It can also support a hydrated, less sticky feel, making it useful when a product needs both good mixing and a pleasant texture.
methylpropanediol.detail: It is a specific glycol, a small liquid molecule used as a formulation helper. Its role can vary with the other ingredients and the amount used.
methylpropanediol.distinctIngredients: Not Propanediol, Propylene Glycol or Butylene Glycol.

mica.name: Mica
mica.summary: Adds slip, reflected light or a pearly effect.
mica.body: Mica is a mineral powder that helps products glide and changes how they reflect light. Depending on its particle size and coatings, it can contribute a soft sheen or a more visible pearly effect.
mica.detail: Mica is often used as the base for layered pigments coated with other minerals. It can also help powders resist clumping, so its job is not always visible sparkle.
mica.aliasNotes: Mica mineral group; does not specify particle size or surface coating.
mica.distinctIngredients: Not automatically interchangeable with Synthetic Fluorphlogopite.

oleth-10.name: Oleth-10
oleth-10.summary: Helps water and oil mix into one product.
oleth-10.body: Oleth-10 helps oily and watery ingredients combine in a cosmetic formula. It is useful when a cream, lotion or cleanser needs a more even mixture.
oleth-10.detail: This mixing role is called emulsifying. Oleth-10 is a specific modified fatty-alcohol ingredient, and its number distinguishes it from other members of the oleth family.
oleth-10.distinctIngredients: Keep separate from other numbered Oleth ingredients and from Oleyl Alcohol.

p-anisic-acid.name: P-Anisic Acid
p-anisic-acid.summary: Helps manage odor and supports protection from spoilage.
p-anisic-acid.body: P-Anisic Acid can help cover unwanted smells in a formula. It is also used for its activity against fungi, contributing to how some products are protected from spoilage.
p-anisic-acid.detail: Its recorded cosmetic function is odor masking, while the editorial explanation describes a preservation-related use from supplier information. That use still depends on the whole preservation system.
p-anisic-acid.aliasNotes: The para form, 4-methoxybenzoic acid; not all anisic-acid forms.

pantolactone.name: Pantolactone
pantolactone.summary: Helps the formula hold on to water.
pantolactone.body: Pantolactone helps a cosmetic formula retain moisture. It is a humectant, meaning an ingredient that holds water, and can support the moisture-focused part of a skin-care product.
pantolactone.detail: It has its own ingredient identity even though its name resembles panthenol. Keep the two separate when reading labels or comparing formulas.
pantolactone.aliasNotes: Pantolactone retained as named; no conversion of stereochemical registry identifiers into separate roster ingredients.
pantolactone.distinctIngredients: Not an alias for Panthenol or Pantothenic Acid.

peg-100-stearate.name: PEG-100 Stearate
peg-100-stearate.summary: Keeps water and oil evenly mixed
peg-100-stearate.body: PEG-100 Stearate helps the watery and oily parts of a cream stay together. This gives the product a consistent texture instead of separate watery and greasy layers.
peg-100-stearate.detail: It is often used alongside glyceryl stearate as part of a combined mixing system.
peg-100-stearate.distinctIngredients: PEG-100 Stearate is a particular PEG stearate grade; retain its number rather than merging it with PEG-30 Stearate.

peg-120-methyl-glucose-dioleate.name: PEG-120 Methyl Glucose Dioleate
peg-120-methyl-glucose-dioleate.summary: Helps oily and watery ingredients mix
peg-120-methyl-glucose-dioleate.body: PEG-120 Methyl Glucose Dioleate helps ingredients that would otherwise separate stay mixed. It supports a more uniform product, so the oil- and water-based parts can be delivered together.
peg-120-methyl-glucose-dioleate.detail: It is a modified sugar-and-fatty-acid ingredient used for its mixing properties.

sources.label: PEG-120 METHYL GLUCOSE DIOLEATE – COSMILE Europe

peg-30-dipolyhydroxystearate.name: PEG-30 Dipolyhydroxystearate
peg-30-dipolyhydroxystearate.summary: Keeps tiny water droplets mixed into oil
peg-30-dipolyhydroxystearate.body: PEG-30 Dipolyhydroxystearate helps make creams in which tiny water droplets sit inside an oily base. It keeps those droplets dispersed, helping the formula stay even and spread smoothly.
peg-30-dipolyhydroxystearate.distinctIngredients: This is PEG-30 Dipolyhydroxystearate, not PEG-30 Stearate; the two have different structures.

peg-30-stearate.name: PEG-30 Stearate
peg-30-stearate.summary: Helps cream ingredients blend and stay mixed
peg-30-stearate.body: PEG-30 Stearate helps water and oil form a blended cream or lotion. Its mixing role supports a consistent texture and helps distribute ingredients throughout the product.
peg-30-stearate.distinctIngredients: Keep PEG-30 Stearate separate from other numbered PEG stearates; the number identifies a different average chain length.

peg-5-glyceryl-triisostearate.name: PEG-5 Glyceryl Triisostearate
peg-5-glyceryl-triisostearate.summary: Helps oils blend with water and spread
peg-5-glyceryl-triisostearate.body: PEG-5 Glyceryl Triisostearate helps oily ingredients mix with water and adds a soft, smooth feel. It can help oil-based cleansing products disperse when water is added.
peg-5-glyceryl-triisostearate.detail: The full name matters: related glyceryl esters and other PEG grades can behave differently.
peg-5-glyceryl-triisostearate.distinctIngredients: Do not treat PEG-5 and PEG-20 Glyceryl Triisostearate as identical, even where supplier keyword lists group them.

sources.label: PEG-5 GLYCERYL TRIISOSTEARATE CAS 86846-21-1 — Unilong Group

peg-6-caprylic-capric-glycerides.name: PEG-6 Caprylic/Capric Glycerides
peg-6-caprylic-capric-glycerides.summary: Helps oily ingredients disperse in water
peg-6-caprylic-capric-glycerides.body: PEG-6 Caprylic/Capric Glycerides helps small amounts of oil blend into water-based products. This makes it useful in micellar cleansing waters and other lightweight formulas that need to handle oily material.

peg-8.name: PEG-8
peg-8.summary: Holds water and helps ingredients dissolve
peg-8.body: PEG-8 attracts water and helps ingredients dissolve in a formula. It can help a product retain moisture while making less water-soluble ingredients easier to include in a water-based blend.
peg-8.distinctIngredients: PEG-8 is not PEG-8 Laurate; adding a fatty-acid ester changes the ingredient's role.

peg-8-laurate.name: PEG-8 Laurate
peg-8-laurate.summary: Helps water mix with oils and grime
peg-8-laurate.body: PEG-8 Laurate is a mixing ingredient that helps oily and watery materials come together. Depending on the formula, it can help stabilize a blend or support cleansing by helping water handle oily residue.

pentaerythrityl-tetra-di-t-butyl-hydroxy.name: Pentaerythrityl Tetra-di-t-butyl Hydroxyhydrocinnamate
pentaerythrityl-tetra-di-t-butyl-hydroxy.summary: Helps protect a product from air-related changes
pentaerythrityl-tetra-di-t-butyl-hydroxy.body: Pentaerythrityl Tetra-di-t-butyl Hydroxyhydrocinnamate helps slow unwanted changes caused by oxidation. It is added to protect the formula, including helping prevent discoloration during storage.
pentaerythrityl-tetra-di-t-butyl-hydroxy.amountAndUse: Its main job here is protecting the product's ingredients during storage.

phenethyl-alcohol.name: Phenethyl Alcohol
phenethyl-alcohol.summary: Softens unwanted odors and supports formula preservation
phenethyl-alcohol.body: Phenethyl Alcohol has a rose-like smell that can cover less pleasant odors from other ingredients. It can also help a product's preservative system limit microbial growth.
phenethyl-alcohol.detail: Its role can be practical as well as aromatic; a small amount may be used to improve how the whole formula smells.

phenylpropanol.name: Phenylpropanol
phenylpropanol.summary: Masks raw-material odors and supports product preservation
phenylpropanol.body: Phenylpropanol helps cover unwanted smells from other ingredients with a faint floral scent. It can also support a preservative system, helping the formula resist microbial growth.

poly-c10-30-alkyl-acrylate.name: Poly C10-30 Alkyl Acrylate
poly-c10-30-alkyl-acrylate.summary: Adjusts thickness and helps a blend stay even
poly-c10-30-alkyl-acrylate.body: Poly C10-30 Alkyl Acrylate helps control how thick or fluid a product feels. It also helps an oil-and-water blend stay stable, supporting a more consistent texture.

sources.label: Poly C10-30 Alkyl Acrylate — COSMILE Europe

polyacrylate-crosspolymer-6.name: Polyacrylate Crosspolymer-6
polyacrylate-crosspolymer-6.summary: Thickens liquids into a smooth gel texture
polyacrylate-crosspolymer-6.body: Polyacrylate Crosspolymer-6 gives watery formulas more body and helps create a gel-like texture. It can also help keep a formula stable and give it a smooth, velvety finish.
polyacrylate-crosspolymer-6.detail: This is a crosslinked polymer: linked chains of repeating units help give the liquid structure while it is spread.

polyethylene.name: Polyethylene
polyethylene.summary: Adds structure and glide to balms and sticks
polyethylene.body: Polyethylene can be used as a waxy ingredient that firms up a balm or stick. It adds body while helping the product glide over skin rather than feeling runny.
polyethylene.detail: Its physical form matters: the same ingredient name does not tell you whether it is present as wax or as solid particles.

polyglycerin-3.name: Polyglycerin-3
polyglycerin-3.summary: Attracts water to support a hydrated feel
polyglycerin-3.body: Polyglycerin-3 is made from linked glycerin units and helps hold onto water. It can support moisture in a formula and help skin feel hydrated after application.
polyglycerin-3.aliasNotes: A glycerin-based ingredient formed from three linked glycerin units.

polyglyceryl-10-stearate.name: Polyglyceryl-10 Stearate
polyglyceryl-10-stearate.summary: Keeps oil and water blended smoothly together
polyglyceryl-10-stearate.body: Polyglyceryl-10 Stearate helps turn oil and water into a stable, smooth mixture. That makes it useful for the texture of creams and lotions, with some added softening feel.
polyglyceryl-10-stearate.distinctIngredients: Retain the complete numbered polyglyceryl ester name; nearby numbers and different fatty-acid endings identify different ingredients.

polyglyceryl-3-polyricinoleate.name: Polyglyceryl-3 Polyricinoleate
polyglyceryl-3-polyricinoleate.summary: Disperses water evenly inside an oily base
polyglyceryl-3-polyricinoleate.body: Polyglyceryl-3 Polyricinoleate helps hold tiny water droplets inside an oil-based mixture. This lets a cream or balm combine watery ingredients with a richer oily base without quickly separating.

polyglyceryl-3-stearate.name: Polyglyceryl-3 Stearate
polyglyceryl-3-stearate.summary: Helps oil and water form a smooth blend
polyglyceryl-3-stearate.body: Polyglyceryl-3 Stearate helps the watery and oily portions of a product mix. It supports a uniform cream or lotion, making ingredients easier to spread together across the skin.
polyglyceryl-3-stearate.distinctIngredients: Retain the complete numbered polyglyceryl ester name; nearby numbers and different fatty-acid endings identify different ingredients.

polyglyceryl-4-isostearate.name: Polyglyceryl-4 Isostearate
polyglyceryl-4-isostearate.summary: Helps keep watery and oily ingredients together
polyglyceryl-4-isostearate.body: Polyglyceryl-4 Isostearate is a mixing ingredient used to combine oil and water. It helps the formula maintain an even texture rather than separating into different layers.
polyglyceryl-4-isostearate.distinctIngredients: Retain the complete numbered polyglyceryl ester name; nearby numbers and different fatty-acid endings identify different ingredients.

polyglyceryl-6-behenate.name: Polyglyceryl-6 Behenate
polyglyceryl-6-behenate.summary: Helps light lotions stay blended and smooth
polyglyceryl-6-behenate.body: Polyglyceryl-6 Behenate helps stabilize products made with both oil and water. It often works with another emulsifier to keep a light lotion or serum evenly blended.
polyglyceryl-6-behenate.distinctIngredients: Retain the complete numbered polyglyceryl ester name; nearby numbers and different fatty-acid endings identify different ingredients.

polyhydroxystearic-acid.name: Polyhydroxystearic Acid
polyhydroxystearic-acid.summary: Helps fine particles spread evenly through formulas
polyhydroxystearic-acid.body: Polyhydroxystearic Acid helps powders and pigments disperse instead of clumping. In makeup and mineral-containing formulas, that can support a more even texture and more uniform application.

polymethylsilsesquioxane.name: Polymethylsilsesquioxane
polymethylsilsesquioxane.summary: Adds a soft, smooth powdery finish
polymethylsilsesquioxane.body: Polymethylsilsesquioxane is a fine powder used to change how a formula feels and looks on skin. It helps create a smooth finish and can soften the appearance of surface texture.
polymethylsilsesquioxane.detail: The visible smoothing is an effect of the powder's finish on the surface.

polyquaternium-10.name: Polyquaternium-10
polyquaternium-10.summary: Adds body and a smooth surface film
polyquaternium-10.body: Polyquaternium-10 helps thicken a formula and leaves a thin film on skin or hair. This can improve the feel of a product and is especially useful for conditioning hair.

polysorbate-20.name: Polysorbate 20
polysorbate-20.summary: Helps small amounts of oil disperse in water
polysorbate-20.body: Polysorbate 20 helps oily ingredients blend into water-based products. It is useful when a formula needs to incorporate ingredients that would otherwise separate or dissolve poorly.
polysorbate-20.detail: This mixing job is especially useful for ingredients that dissolve more readily in oil than in water.
polysorbate-20.distinctIngredients: Polysorbates 20, 60 and 80 are distinct ingredients, not interchangeable names or a ranking of product quality.

polysorbate-60.name: Polysorbate 60
polysorbate-60.summary: Helps water and oil stay evenly mixed
polysorbate-60.body: Polysorbate 60 helps the water- and oil-based parts of a formula come together. It supports an even cream or lotion texture so the product spreads as one blended mixture.
polysorbate-60.distinctIngredients: Polysorbates 20, 60 and 80 are distinct ingredients, not interchangeable names or a ranking of product quality.

polysorbate-80.name: Polysorbate 80
polysorbate-80.summary: Keeps oily and watery ingredients blended together
polysorbate-80.body: Polysorbate 80 helps combine oil and water into an even mixture. It is used to support the texture and stability of products that need both water-based and oily ingredients.
polysorbate-80.distinctIngredients: Polysorbates 20, 60 and 80 are distinct ingredients, not interchangeable names or a ranking of product quality.

polyvinyl-alcohol.name: Polyvinyl Alcohol
polyvinyl-alcohol.summary: Forms a thin film and adjusts texture
polyvinyl-alcohol.body: Polyvinyl Alcohol helps form a continuous film as a product dries. It also adjusts thickness, helping a formula hold together and achieve the intended consistency.

potassium-azeloyl-diglycinate.name: Potassium Azeloyl Diglycinate
potassium-azeloyl-diglycinate.summary: Supports a hydrated feel in water-based formulas
potassium-azeloyl-diglycinate.body: Potassium Azeloyl Diglycinate is a water-soluble skin-conditioning ingredient made from azelaic acid and glycine. It is used for a hydrated skin feel and can fit into light, water-based formulas.
potassium-azeloyl-diglycinate.evidence: It is a different molecule from azelaic acid, so evidence for azelaic acid cannot establish the same effects for this ingredient.

potassium-cetyl-phosphate.name: Potassium Cetyl Phosphate
potassium-cetyl-phosphate.summary: Helps watery and oily ingredients stay blended
potassium-cetyl-phosphate.body: Potassium Cetyl Phosphate helps stabilize products containing both oil and water. Its job is to keep the mixture even, supporting a consistent texture and application.

potassium-chloride.name: Potassium Chloride
potassium-chloride.summary: Helps adjust how thick a product feels
potassium-chloride.body: Potassium Chloride is a salt used to fine-tune a product's consistency. It can help a formula reach the right thickness so it pours, spreads or stays in place as intended.

potassium-sorbate.name: Potassium Sorbate
potassium-sorbate.summary: Helps limit yeast and mold in formulas
potassium-sorbate.body: Potassium Sorbate helps keep a product from spoiling, particularly by limiting yeast and mold. It usually works as one part of a broader preservation system.
potassium-sorbate.detail: Its performance depends on the formula's acidity, so the full preservative system matters more than this ingredient alone.

propanediol.name: Propanediol
propanediol.summary: Holds water and helps other ingredients dissolve
propanediol.body: Propanediol helps attract water and dissolve other ingredients in a formula. It can improve skin feel and support a product's preservative system, making it a useful multitasking liquid.
propanediol.distinctIngredients: Propanediol and Propylene Glycol are distinct cosmetic ingredient names; keep them separate.

propylene-carbonate.name: Propylene Carbonate
propylene-carbonate.summary: Helps ingredients dissolve and fine-tunes product thickness
propylene-carbonate.body: Propylene Carbonate helps dissolve ingredients that need a suitable liquid carrier. It can also change how thick or fluid a product feels, supporting a workable, evenly blended formula.

propylene-glycol.name: Propylene Glycol
propylene-glycol.summary: Attracts water and helps ingredients dissolve evenly
propylene-glycol.body: Propylene Glycol helps hold water and dissolve other ingredients. It can support a hydrated skin feel while helping the formula remain evenly mixed and maintain its texture.
propylene-glycol.caution: It can cause irritation or contact allergy in some people. If patch testing has confirmed an allergy to propylene glycol, avoid products that contain it.

sources.label: Contact allergy to propylene glycol — DermNet

propylparaben.name: Propylparaben
propylparaben.summary: Helps stop unwanted microbes growing in products
propylparaben.body: Propylparaben is a preservative that helps protect a formula from microbial spoilage. It contributes to keeping the product usable through storage and repeated opening.

pullulan.name: Pullulan
pullulan.summary: Forms a flexible film and smooths texture
pullulan.body: Pullulan is a sugar-based polymer that forms a thin, flexible film on skin. It can help a formula feel smooth, add thickness and help create peel-off textures.
pullulan.detail: Any immediate tightening sensation comes from the surface film.
pullulan.amountAndUse: The film-forming role is useful in peel-off products and formulas designed to leave a smooth surface finish.

sclerotium-gum.name: Sclerotium Gum
sclerotium-gum.summary: Thickens watery formulas and helps keep mixtures stable
sclerotium-gum.body: Sclerotium Gum gives watery products a thicker, gel-like consistency. It can also help keep oil-and-water mixtures stable and is often combined with other gums to shape the texture.

sebacic-acid.name: Sebacic Acid
sebacic-acid.summary: Helps keep a formula's acidity under control
sebacic-acid.body: Sebacic Acid helps control a product's acidity, also called its pH. This is a behind-the-scenes formulation job that helps the ingredients work within the intended conditions.

silica.name: Silica
silica.summary: Absorbs oil and gives products more body
silica.body: Silica is a powder used to absorb oil and adjust texture. It can help a formula leave a less shiny finish or keep fine particles evenly suspended.
silica.aliasNotes: Silica is silicon dioxide; cosmetic grades and particle properties vary.

silica-silylate.name: Silica Silylate
silica-silylate.summary: Soaks up oil and thickens oily formulas
silica-silylate.body: Silica Silylate is a treated silica powder that absorbs oily material. It can reduce a greasy-looking finish and help give the oily part of a formula more structure.
silica-silylate.distinctIngredients: Silica Silylate is chemically surface-treated silica; keep it separate from unmodified Silica.

simethicone.name: Simethicone
simethicone.summary: Reduces unwanted bubbles and improves formula handling
simethicone.body: Simethicone helps stop unwanted foam forming while a product is made or used. It can also help coat and spread fine particles, supporting a more uniform formula.
simethicone.aliasNotes: A silicone-and-silica material; not a separate name for plain Dimethicone.

sodium-acryloyldimethyltaurate-vp-crossp.name: Sodium Acryloyldimethyltaurate/VP Crosspolymer
sodium-acryloyldimethyltaurate-vp-crossp.summary: Helps an oil-and-water blend stay consistent
sodium-acryloyldimethyltaurate-vp-crossp.body: Sodium Acryloyldimethyltaurate/VP Crosspolymer helps keep mixed oil-and-water formulas stable. It supports an even product texture instead of allowing the different parts to separate.
sodium-acryloyldimethyltaurate-vp-crossp.distinctIngredients: Keep this sodium crosspolymer separate from similarly named ammonium polymers and from non-crosslinked copolymers.

sodium-anisate.name: Sodium Anisate
sodium-anisate.summary: Helps limit unwanted microbial growth in formulas
sodium-anisate.body: Sodium Anisate can help control the growth of microbes in a product. It is used as part of formulation systems designed to keep the product stable and resist spoilage.

sodium-benzoate.name: Sodium Benzoate
sodium-benzoate.summary: Helps protect products from unwanted microbial growth
sodium-benzoate.body: Sodium Benzoate helps keep a product from spoiling, especially by limiting fungi. It commonly works with other preservatives to protect the formula during storage and use.
sodium-benzoate.detail: Its effectiveness depends on the product's acidity and the other ingredients in its preservation system.

sodium-cetearyl-sulfate.name: Sodium Cetearyl Sulfate
sodium-cetearyl-sulfate.summary: Helps water lift away oily residue
sodium-cetearyl-sulfate.body: Sodium Cetearyl Sulfate is a cleansing ingredient that helps water interact with oils and dirt. It can also help form foam, contributing to the feel of a wash.

sodium-chloride.name: Sodium Chloride
sodium-chloride.summary: Fine-tunes thickness in cleansing and lotion formulas
sodium-chloride.body: Sodium Chloride is the same chemical substance as table salt. In skincare, it often helps adjust a cleanser's thickness or stabilize a mixture rather than acting as a skin treatment.
sodium-chloride.detail: Its form changes its job: dissolved salt helps shape texture, while undissolved grains can provide physical scrubbing.

sodium-citrate.name: Sodium Citrate
sodium-citrate.summary: Balances acidity and binds troublesome metal traces
sodium-citrate.body: Sodium Citrate helps control a product's acidity and binds tiny traces of metals in the formula. Those jobs help the mixture stay consistent during storage.

sodium-cocoyl-glutamate.name: Sodium Cocoyl Glutamate
sodium-cocoyl-glutamate.summary: Helps a cleanser lift oils and everyday dirt
sodium-cocoyl-glutamate.body: Sodium Cocoyl Glutamate helps remove oily residue and dirt with water. It is often combined with other cleansing ingredients to build the product's overall washing action and feel.

sodium-cocoyl-glycinate.name: Sodium Cocoyl Glycinate
sodium-cocoyl-glycinate.summary: Helps water wash away oils and residue
sodium-cocoyl-glycinate.body: Sodium Cocoyl Glycinate is a cleansing ingredient made using glycine and fatty-acid components. It helps a wash remove oily material and is often part of a blended cleansing system.
sodium-cocoyl-glycinate.distinctIngredients: Sodium Cocoyl Glycinate and Sodium Cocoyl Glutamate are different amino-acid-derived cleansing ingredients.

sodium-cocoyl-isethionate.name: Sodium Cocoyl Isethionate
sodium-cocoyl-isethionate.summary: Lifts oily residue and creates creamy lather
sodium-cocoyl-isethionate.body: Sodium Cocoyl Isethionate helps wash away oils and dirt while creating a creamy lather. It is widely used in cleansing bars made with detergents rather than traditional soap.

sodium-dodecylbenzenesulfonate.name: Sodium Dodecylbenzenesulfonate
sodium-dodecylbenzenesulfonate.summary: Helps oily residue mix with rinse water
sodium-dodecylbenzenesulfonate.body: Sodium Dodecylbenzenesulfonate is a cleansing ingredient that helps water carry away oily material. Its surface-active properties allow substances that resist water alone to be more easily dispersed.

sodium-gluconate.name: Sodium Gluconate
sodium-gluconate.summary: Binds metal traces that can change a formula
sodium-gluconate.body: Sodium Gluconate helps capture tiny amounts of metals in a product. This helps reduce unwanted changes such as discoloration or deterioration of oils during storage.

sodium-hydroxide.name: Sodium Hydroxide
sodium-hydroxide.summary: Raises a formula's pH to its intended level
sodium-hydroxide.body: Sodium Hydroxide is used to reduce a formula's acidity, bringing its pH into the intended range. It can also react with fats during soapmaking.
sodium-hydroxide.detail: In a finished formula, its role and the final pH matter; seeing the name alone does not tell you how alkaline the product is.

sodium-laureth-sulfate.name: Sodium Laureth Sulfate
sodium-laureth-sulfate.summary: Lifts oil and dirt while creating foam
sodium-laureth-sulfate.body: Sodium Laureth Sulfate helps water wash away oils and dirt and produces a bubbly lather. It is commonly combined with other ingredients to build the texture and washing feel of a cleanser.
sodium-laureth-sulfate.distinctIngredients: Sodium Laureth Sulfate (SLES) is not Sodium Lauryl Sulfate (SLS).

sodium-lauroyl-sarcosinate.name: Sodium Lauroyl Sarcosinate
sodium-lauroyl-sarcosinate.summary: Helps remove residue and build a lather
sodium-lauroyl-sarcosinate.body: Sodium Lauroyl Sarcosinate helps a cleanser lift oils and dirt from skin. It also supports foaming and is often combined with other cleansing ingredients to shape the wash's feel.

sodium-levulinate.name: Sodium Levulinate
sodium-levulinate.summary: Supports skin feel and paired preservation systems
sodium-levulinate.body: Sodium Levulinate is a skin-conditioning ingredient that is also used in preservation blends. Paired with ingredients such as sodium anisate, it helps build systems that protect a formula from microbial spoilage.
sodium-levulinate.amountAndUse: Its preservation role depends on the partner ingredients and the formula's acidity.

sodium-metabisulfite.name: Sodium Metabisulfite
sodium-metabisulfite.summary: Helps prevent oxidation and unwanted formula changes
sodium-metabisulfite.body: Sodium Metabisulfite helps slow oxidation, a process that can change a product's color or ingredients over time. It can also contribute to protecting the formula from microbial spoilage.
sodium-metabisulfite.caution: If you have a confirmed contact allergy to sodium metabisulfite, avoid skincare containing it and follow your clinician's advice about related sulfites.

sources.label: Sodium metabisulfite — British Society for Cutaneous Allergy

sodium-phosphate.name: Sodium Phosphate
sodium-phosphate.summary: Helps keep a product's acidity steady
